text: General George Washington hoists the first United States flag, the Grand Union Flag, at Prospect Hill.
name: George Washington

text: Boris Bazhanov defects through Iran to seek asylum in France. He is the only member of Joseph Stalin's secretariat to have defected from the Soviet Union.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Cuban Revolution: Fulgencio Batista, dictator of Cuba, is overthrown by Fidel Castro's forces.
name: Fulgencio Batista

text: Empress Maria Theresa of Austria amends the Constitutio Criminalis Theresiana to include the abolition of torture throughout the Habsburg-ruled countries of Austria and Bohemia.
name: Maria Theresa of Austria

text: American Revolutionary War: American forces under the command of General George Washington repulse a British attack led by General Charles Cornwallis at the Battle of the Assunpink Creek near Trenton, New Jersey.
name: George Washington

text: World premiere of the science fiction play R.U.R. by the Czech writer Karel Čapek in a theater in Hradec Králové.
name: Karel Čapek

text: Ronald Reagan, past movie actor and future President of the United States, is sworn in as Governor of California.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Pope Leo X excommunicates Martin Luther in the papal bull Decet Romanum Pontificem.
name: Martin Luther

text: American Revolutionary War: American forces under General George Washington defeat British forces at the Battle of Princeton, helping boost patriot morale.
name: George Washington

text: A gun battle in the East End of London leaves two dead. It sparked a political row over the involvement of then-Home Secretary Winston Churchill.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Pope John XXIII excommunicates Fidel Castro.
name: Pope John XXIII

text: Louis XV of France survives an assassination attempt by Robert-François Damiens, who becomes the last person to be executed in France by drawing and quartering (the traditional form of capital punishment used for regicides).
name: Louis XV of France

text: Dreyfus affair: French army officer Alfred Dreyfus is stripped of his rank and sentenced to life imprisonment on Devil's Island.
name: Alfred Dreyfus

text: The sixth All-Russian Conference of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party (Prague Party Conference) opens. In the course of the conference, Vladimir Lenin and his supporters break from the rest of the party to form the Bolshevik movement.
name: Vladimir Lenin

text: Alexander Dubček comes to power in Czechoslovakia, effectively beginning the "Prague Spring".
name: Alexander Dubček

text: King Henry VIII of England marries Anne of Cleves.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: The Union of Arras unites the southern Netherlands under the Duke of Parma (Ottavio Farnese), governor in the name of King Philip II of Spain.
name: Philip II of Spain

text: Maria Montessori opens her first school and daycare center for working class children in Rome, Italy.
name: Maria Montessori

text: German geophysicist Alfred Wegener first presents his theory of continental drift.
name: Alfred Wegener

text: Mother Teresa arrives by sea in Calcutta, India, to begin her work among India's poorest and sick people.
name: Mother Teresa

text: Galileo Galilei makes his first observation of the four Galilean moons: Ganymede, Callisto, Io and Europa, although he is not able to distinguish the last two until the following night.
name: Galileo Galilei

text: HMS Beagle, with Charles Darwin on board, drops anchor off the Chonos Archipelago.
name: Charles Darwin

text: Benito Mussolini and French Foreign Minister Pierre Laval sign the Franco-Italian Agreement.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: The United States recognizes the new Cuban government of Fidel Castro.
name: Fidel Castro

text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter authorizes legislation giving $1.5 billion in loans to bail out the Chrysler Corporation.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: The premiere of George Frideric Handel's Ariodante takes place at the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: George Washington delivers the first State of the Union address in New York City.
name: George Washington

text: President Lyndon B. Johnson declares a "War on Poverty" in the United States.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Humphry Davy tests his safety lamp for miners at Hebburn Colliery.
name: Humphry Davy

text: President of Egypt Gamal Abdel Nasser opens construction on the Aswan Dam by detonating ten tons of dynamite to demolish twenty tons of granite on the east bank of the Nile.
name: Gamal Abdel Nasser

text: William Herschel discovers Titania and Oberon, two moons of Uranus.
name: William Herschel

text: Enver Hoxha, Secretary General of the Communist Party of Albania, declares the People's Republic of Albania with himself as head of state.
name: Enver Hoxha

text: Gustav I of Sweden is crowned King of Sweden, having already reigned since his election in June 1523.
name: Gustav I of Sweden

text: Lyndon B. Johnson states that the United States should stay in South Vietnam until Communist aggression there is ended.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: The Harrisburg Seven: Rev. Philip Berrigan and five other activists are indicted on charges of conspiring to kidnap Henry Kissinger and of plotting to blow up the heating tunnels of federal buildings in Washington, D.C.
name: Henry Kissinger

text: Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, is sentenced to death for treason, on the grounds of having quartered his arms to make them similar to those of the King, Henry VIII of England.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Émile Zola's J'accuse…! exposes the Dreyfus affair.
name: Émile Zola

text: King Henry III of England marries Eleanor of Provence.
name: Henry III of England

text: The Battle of Rivoli is fought with a decisive French victory by Napoleon Bonaparte, marking the beginning of the end of the War of the First Coalition and the start of French hegemony over Italy for two decades.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Giacomo Puccini's Tosca opens in Rome.
name: Giacomo Puccini

text: Roald Amundsen's South Pole expedition makes landfall on the eastern edge of the Ross Ice Shelf.
name: Roald Amundsen

text: World War II: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill begin the Casablanca Conference to discuss strategy and study the next phase of the war.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Josip Broz Tito is elected the first President of Yugoslavia.
name: Josip Broz Tito

text: King Francis I of France gives Jean-François Roberval a commission to settle the province of New France (Canada) and provide for the spread of the "Holy Catholic faith".
name: Francis I of France

text: A paper by David Brewster is read to the Royal Society, belatedly announcing his discovery of what we now call the biaxial class of doubly-refracting crystals. On the same day, Augustin-Jean Fresnel signs a "supplement" (submitted four days later) on reflection of polarized light.
name: Augustin-Jean Fresnel

text: Construction ends on the Buffalo Bill Dam in Wyoming, United States, which was the highest dam in the world at the time, at 99 m (325 ft).
name: Buffalo Bill

text: Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht, two of the most prominent communists in Germany, are clubbed and then shot to death by members of the Freikorps at the end of the Spartacist uprising.
name: Rosa Luxemburg

text: Pope John Paul II receives a delegation from the Polish trade union Solidarity at the Vatican led by Lech Wałęsa.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: The first edition of El ingenioso hidalgo Don Quijote de la Mancha (Book One of Don Quixote) by Miguel de Cervantes is published in Madrid, Spain.
name: Miguel de Cervantes

text: King Philip V of Spain promulgates the Nueva Planta decree of the Principality of Catalonia, abolishing the Catalan institutions and its legal system, being replaced by those of the Castile, thus putting an end to Catalonia as separate state and becoming a province of the new French-style Kingdom of Spain.
name: Philip V of Spain

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler moves into his underground bunker, the so-called Führerbunker.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: During the French Wars of Religion, Henry IV of France declares war on Spain.
name: Henry IV of France

text: Captain James Cook leads the first expedition to sail south of the Antarctic Circle.
name: James Cook

text: Anton Chekhov's The Cherry Orchard receives its premiere performance at the Moscow Art Theatre.
name: Anton Chekhov

text: British polar explorer Captain Robert Falcon Scott reaches the South Pole, one month after Roald Amundsen.
name: Roald Amundsen

text: Pope Pius IV reopens the Council of Trent for its third and final session.
name: Pope Pius IV

text: James Cook is the first known European to discover the Hawaiian Islands, which he names the "Sandwich Islands".
name: James Cook

text: Hundred Years' War: Rouen surrenders to Henry V of England, completing his reconquest of Normandy.
name: Henry V of England

text: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's Faust: The First Part of the Tragedy receives its premiere performance.
name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

text: Giuseppe Verdi's opera Il trovatore receives its premiere performance in Rome.
name: Giuseppe Verdi

text: John F. Kennedy is inaugurated as the 35th President of the United States of America, becoming the youngest man to be elected into that office, and the first Roman Catholic.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Twenty minutes after Ronald Reagan is inaugurated as the 40th President of the United States of America, Iran releases 52 American hostages.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: After being found guilty of treason by the French National Convention, Louis XVI of France is executed by guillotine.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: The Boeing 747, the world's first "jumbo jet", enters commercial service for launch customer Pan American Airways with its maiden voyage from New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport to London Heathrow Airport.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: In the conflict between King Henry III of England and his rebellious barons led by Simon de Montfort, King Louis IX of France issues the Mise of Amiens, a one-sided decision in favour of Henry that later leads to the Second Barons' War.
name: Henry III of England

text: Blaise Pascal publishes the first of his Lettres provinciales.
name: Blaise Pascal

text: The trial of the anti-Soviet Trotskyist center sees seventeen mid-level Communists accused of sympathizing with Leon Trotsky and plotting to overthrow Joseph Stalin's regime.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Charles Lindbergh testifies before the U.S. Congress and recommends that the United States negotiate a neutrality pact with Adolf Hitler.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: World War II: German admiral Karl Dönitz launches Operation Hannibal.
name: Karl Dönitz

text: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducts its first members: Little Richard, Chuck Berry, James Brown, Ray Charles, Sam Cooke, Fats Domino, The Everly Brothers, Buddy Holly, Jerry Lee Lewis and Elvis Presley.
name: Ray Charles

text: Coronation of Francis I of France takes place at Reims Cathedral, where the new monarch is anointed with the oil of Clovis and girt with the sword of Charlemagne.
name: Francis I of France

text: Henry VIII of England secretly marries his second wife Anne Boleyn.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Battle of Mikatagahara: In Japan, Takeda Shingen defeats Tokugawa Ieyasu.
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: Thomas Edison and Alexander Graham Bell form the Oriental Telephone Company.
name: Alexander Graham Bell

text: Richard Strauss's opera Elektra receives its debut performance at the Dresden State Opera.
name: Richard Strauss

text: Alexander Graham Bell inaugurates U.S. transcontinental telephone service, speaking from New York to Thomas Watson in San Francisco.
name: Alexander Graham Bell

text: Pope Pius XII elevates the Apostolic Vicariate of the Hawaiian Islands to the dignity of a diocese. It becomes the Roman Catholic Diocese of Honolulu.
name: Pope Pius XII

text: In Washington, D.C., US President John F. Kennedy delivers the first live presidential television news conference.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Charles Manson and four "Family" members (three of them female) are found guilty of the 1969 Tate-LaBianca murders.
name: Charles Manson

text: Pope John Paul II starts his first official papal visits outside Italy to The Bahamas, Dominican Republic, and Mexico.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Mother Teresa is honored with India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna.
name: Mother Teresa

text: During a historic visit to Cuba, Pope John Paul II demands political reforms and the release of political prisoners while condemning US attempts to isolate the country.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Spanish Civil War: Catalonia Offensive: Troops loyal to nationalist General Francisco Franco and aided by Italy take Barcelona.
name: Francisco Franco

text: The Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory sees first light under the direction of Edwin Hubble, becoming the largest aperture optical telescope (until BTA-6 is built in 1976).
name: Edwin Hubble

text: King Charles VI of France was nearly killed when several other dancers' costumes caught fire during a masquerade ball in Paris.
name: Charles VI of France

text: Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice is first published in the United Kingdom.
name: Jane Austen

text: Ronald Reagan lifts remaining domestic petroleum price and allocation controls in the United States, helping to end the 1979 energy crisis and begin the 1980s oil glut.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Charles I of England is executed in Whitehall, London.
name: Charles I of England

text: Oliver Cromwell, Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of England, is ritually executed more than two years after his death, on the 12th anniversary of the execution of the monarch he himself deposed.
name: Oliver Cromwell

text: Adolf Hitler's rise to power: Hitler takes office as the Chancellor of Germany.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: During a speech in the Reichstag, Adolf Hitler makes a prediction about the end of the Jewish race in Europe if another world war were to occur.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Following the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi in his home compound, India's prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, broadcasts to the nation, saying "The light has gone out of our lives". The date of the assassination becomes observed as "Martyrs' Day" in India.
name: Mahatma Gandhi

text: The Mudéjar of Murcia, who had rebelled against the Crown of Castile during the Mudéjar revolt of 1264-1266, surrender the city to James I of Aragon after a siege lasting a month.
name: James I of Aragon

text: Anton Chekhov's Three Sisters premieres at Moscow Art Theatre in Russia.
name: Anton Chekhov

text: Leon Trotsky is exiled to Alma-Ata.
name: Leon Trotsky

text: World War II: German field marshal Friedrich Paulus surrenders to the Soviets at Stalingrad, followed two days later by the remainder of his Sixth Army, ending one of the war's fiercest battles.
name: Friedrich Paulus

text: President Abraham Lincoln signs the Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: World War II: Josef Terboven, Reichskommissar of German-occupied Norway, appoints Vidkun Quisling the Minister President of the National Government.
name: Vidkun Quisling

text: The Osvald Group is responsible for the first, active event of anti-Nazi resistance in Norway, to protest the inauguration of Vidkun Quisling.
name: Vidkun Quisling

text: Adolf Hitler announces that the expansion of Lebensraum into Eastern Europe, and its ruthless Germanisation, are the ultimate geopolitical objectives of Nazi foreign policy.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Following the death of the Roman Emperor Septimius Severus at Eboracum (modern York, England) while preparing to lead a campaign against the Caledonians, the empire is left in the control of his two quarrelling sons, Caracalla and Geta, whom he had instructed to make peace.
name: Septimius Severus

text: John Rogers is burned at the stake, becoming the first English Protestant martyr under Mary I of England.
name: Mary I of England

text: George Washington is unanimously elected as the first President of the United States by the U.S. Electoral College.
name: George Washington

text: Adolf Hitler appoints himself as head of the Armed Forces High Command.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Generalísimo Francisco Franco becomes the 68th "Caudillo de España", or Leader of Spain.
name: Francisco Franco

text: Gamal Abdel Nasser is nominated to be the first president of the United Arab Republic.
name: Gamal Abdel Nasser

text: James II of England and VII of Scotland is proclaimed King upon the death of his brother Charles II.
name: James II of England

text: Washington National Airport is renamed Ronald Reagan National Airport.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Edward of Caernarvon (later King Edward II of England) becomes the first English Prince of Wales.
name: Edward II of England

text: In Florence, Italy, supporters of Girolamo Savonarola burn cosmetics, art, and books, in a "Bonfire of the vanities".
name: Girolamo Savonarola

text: Dreyfus affair: Émile Zola is brought to trial for libel for publishing J'Accuse...!
name: Émile Zola

text: The Beatles land in the United States for the first time, at the newly renamed John F. Kennedy International Airport.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Delaware refuses to ratify the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, delaying the criminalization of slavery until the amendment's national adoption on December 6, 1865. The amendment is ultimately ratified by Delaware on February 12, 1901, the 92nd anniversary of Abraham Lincoln's birth.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Gaetano Donizetti's opera La fille du régiment receives its first performance in Paris, France.
name: Gaetano Donizetti

text: Giuseppe Verdi's opera I Lombardi alla prima crociata receives its first performance in Milan, Italy.
name: Giuseppe Verdi

text: Anton Bruckner's 9th Symphony receives its first performance in Vienna, Austria.
name: Anton Bruckner

text: Pope Pius X publishes the encyclical Vehementer Nos.
name: Pope Pius X

text: BBC Television produces the world's first ever science fiction television programme, an adaptation of a section of the Karel Čapek play R.U.R., that coined the term "robot".
name: Karel Čapek

text: The Vatican confirmed that Pope Benedict XVI would resign the papacy as a result of his advanced age.
name: Pope Benedict XVI

text: Antonín Dvořák's Jakobín is premiered at National Theater in Prague
name: Antonín Dvořák

text: The trial of Slobodan Milošević, the former President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, begins at the United Nations International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague, Netherlands. He dies four years later before its conclusion.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: Catherine Howard, the fifth wife of Henry VIII of England, is executed for adultery.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Galileo Galilei arrives in Rome for his trial before the Inquisition.
name: Galileo Galilei

text: The delegation headed by Metropolitan bishop Andrei Șaguna hands out to the Emperor Franz Joseph I of Austria the General Petition of Romanian leaders in Transylvania, Banat and Bukovina, which demands that the Romanian nation be recognized.
name: Franz Joseph I of Austria

text: A jury in Flemington, New Jersey finds Bruno Hauptmann guilty of the 1932 kidnapping and murder of the Lindbergh baby, the son of Charles Lindbergh.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: Konstantin Chernenko succeeds the late Yuri Andropov as general secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.
name: Konstantin Chernenko

text: Having been declared a heretic and laicized by Pope Paul IV on 4 December 1555, Archbishop of Canterbury Thomas Cranmer is publicly defrocked at Christ Church Cathedral.
name: Pope Paul IV

text: James Cook is killed by Native Hawaiians near Kealakekua on the Island of Hawaii.
name: James Cook

text: Alexander Graham Bell applies for a patent for the telephone, as does Elisha Gray.
name: Alexander Graham Bell

text: Saint Valentine's Day Massacre: Seven people, six of them gangster rivals of Al Capone's gang, are murdered in Chicago.
name: Al Capone

text: Tsar Nicholas II of Russia issues a declaration known as the February Manifesto, which reduces the autonomy of the Grand Duchy of Finland, thus beginning the first period of oppression.
name: Nicholas II of Russia

text: King George VI of the United Kingdom is buried in St George's Chapel, Windsor Castle.
name: George VI of the United Kingdom

text: Andrew of Longjumeau is dispatched by Louis IX of France as his ambassador to meet with the Khagan of the Mongol Empire.
name: Louis IX of France

text: Fidel Castro becomes Premier of Cuba after dictator Fulgencio Batista was overthrown on January 1.
name: Fulgencio Batista

text: Emperor Septimius Severus defeats usurper Clodius Albinus in the Battle of Lugdunum, the bloodiest battle between Roman armies.
name: Septimius Severus

text: Ezra Pound is awarded the first Bollingen Prize in poetry by the Bollingen Foundation and Yale University.
name: Ezra Pound

text: The Postal Service Act, establishing the United States Post Office Department, is signed by United States President George Washington.
name: George Washington

text: Louis-Alexandre Berthier removes Pope Pius VI from power.
name: Pope Pius VI

text: Adolf Hitler secretly meets with German industrialists to arrange for financing of the Nazi Party's upcoming election campaign.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: In the Albanian capital Tirana, a gigantic statue of Albania's long-time leader, Enver Hoxha, is brought down by mobs of angry protesters.
name: Enver Hoxha

text: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish The Communist Manifesto.
name: Friedrich Engels

text: The British government, under Winston Churchill, abolishes identity cards in the UK to "set the people free".
name: Winston Churchill

text: In the prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine Russian President Vladimir Putin declares the Luhansk People's Republic and Donetsk People's Republic as independent from Ukraine, and moves troops into the region. The action is condemned by the United Nations.
name: Vladimir Putin

text: King Charles VIII of France enters Naples to claim the city's throne.
name: Charles VIII of France

text: Empress Wu Zetian abdicates the throne, restoring the Tang dynasty.
name: Wu Zetian

text: Mexican-American War: Battle of Buena Vista: In Mexico, American troops under future president General Zachary Taylor defeat Mexican General Antonio López de Santa Anna.
name: Antonio López de Santa Anna

text: President-elect Abraham Lincoln arrives secretly in Washington, D.C., after the thwarting of an alleged assassination plot in Baltimore, Maryland.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Émile Zola is imprisoned in France after writing J'Accuse…!, a letter accusing the French government of antisemitism and wrongfully imprisoning Captain Alfred Dreyfus.
name: Alfred Dreyfus

text: German theoretical physicist Werner Heisenberg writes a letter to fellow physicist Wolfgang Pauli, in which he describes his uncertainty principle for the first time.
name: Wolfgang Pauli

text: Five-time Argentine Formula One champion Juan Manuel Fangio is kidnapped by rebels involved in the Cuban Revolution, on the eve of the Cuban Grand Prix. He was released the following day after the race.
name: Juan Manuel Fangio

text: Saddam Hussein begins the Anfal genocide against Kurds and Assyrians in northern Iraq.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: With the papal bull Inter gravissimas, Pope Gregory XIII announces the Gregorian calendar.
name: Pope Gregory XIII

text: L'Orfeo by Claudio Monteverdi, one of the first works recognized as an opera, receives its première performance.
name: Claudio Monteverdi

text: Rinaldo by George Frideric Handel, the first Italian opera written for the London stage, is premièred.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: Treaty of Paris between Napoleon and Frederick William III of Prussia against Russia is signed.
name: Frederick William III of Prussia

text: The stage première of Peer Gynt, a play by Henrik Ibsen with incidental music by Edvard Grieg, takes place in Christiania (Oslo), Norway.
name: Edvard Grieg

text: The Nazi Party (NSDAP) was founded by Adolf Hitler in the Hofbräuhaus beer hall in Munich, Germany.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Fidel Castro retires as the President of Cuba and the Council of Ministers after 32 years. He remained as head of the Communist Party for another three years.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Russo-Ukrainian War: Days after recognising Donetsk and Luhansk as independent states, Russian president Vladimir Putin orders a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
name: Vladimir Putin

text: Roman emperor Hadrian adopts Antoninus Pius as his son, effectively making him his successor.
name: Antoninus Pius

text: George Frideric Handel's opera Nero premiered in Hamburg.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: Adolf Hitler, having been stateless for seven years, obtains German citizenship when he is appointed a Brunswick state official by Dietrich Klagges, a fellow Nazi. As a result, Hitler is able to run for Reichspräsident in the 1932 election.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Galileo Galilei is formally banned by the Roman Catholic Church from teaching or defending the view that the earth orbits the sun.
name: Galileo Galilei

text: Napoleon Bonaparte escapes from exile on the island of Elba.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Adolf Hitler orders the Luftwaffe to be re-formed, violating the provisions of the Treaty of Versailles.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: U.N. Secretary-General U Thant signs United Nations proclamation of the vernal equinox as Earth Day.
name: U Thant

text: Iran-Contra affair: The Tower Commission rebukes President Ronald Reagan for not controlling his national security staff.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Abraham Lincoln makes a speech at Cooper Union in the city of New York that plays an important role in his election to the Presidency.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Olof Palme, 26th Prime Minister of Sweden, is assassinated in Stockholm.
name: Olof Palme

text: Pope Benedict XVI resigns as the pope of the Catholic Church, becoming the first pope to do so since Pope Gregory XII in 1415.
name: Pope Benedict XVI

text: Writs issued in February by Charles I of England mandate that every county in England (not just seaport towns) pay ship tax by this date.
name: Charles I of England

text: Samuel de Champlain reclaims his role as commander of New France on behalf of Cardinal Richelieu.
name: Cardinal Richelieu

text: Leaders of the Mamluk dynasty are killed by Egyptian ruler Muhammad Ali.
name: Muhammad Ali

text: Electrical engineer Nikola Tesla gives the first public demonstration of radio in St. Louis, Missouri.
name: Nikola Tesla

text: Aviator Charles Lindbergh's 20-month-old son Charles Jr is kidnapped from his home in East Amwell, New Jersey. His body would not be found until May 12.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin suffers a stroke and collapses; he dies four days later.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Uprisings against Saddam Hussein begin in Iraq, leading to the deaths of more than 25,000 people, mostly civilians.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: The Olympic Theatre, designed by Andrea Palladio, is inaugurated in Vicenza.
name: Andrea Palladio

text: Alexander II of Russia signs the Emancipation Manifesto, freeing serfs.
name: Alexander II of Russia

text: Pope Leo XIII reestablishes the Catholic Church in Scotland, recreating sees and naming bishops for the first time since 1603.
name: Pope Leo XIII

text: Adolf Hitler's Nazi Party receives 43.9% at the Reichstag elections, which allows the Nazis to later pass the Enabling Act and establish a dictatorship.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Six high-ranking members of the Soviet politburo, including Joseph Stalin, sign an order for the execution of 25,700 Polish intelligentsia, including 14,700 Polish POWs, in what will become known as the Katyn massacre.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Cold War: Winston Churchill delivers his famous "Iron Curtain" speech at Westminster College, Missouri.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Joseph Stalin, the longest serving leader of the Soviet Union, dies at his Volynskoe dacha in Moscow after suffering a cerebral hemorrhage four days earlier.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Dmitri Mendeleev presents the first periodic table to the Russian Chemical Society.
name: Dmitri Mendeleev

text: World War II: Generalfeldmarschall Erwin Rommel launches the Battle of Medenine in an attempt to slow down the British Eighth Army. It fails, and he leaves Africa three days later.
name: Erwin Rommel

text: Georgy Malenkov succeeds Joseph Stalin as Premier of the Soviet Union and First Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Cold War: Joseph Stalin's daughter Svetlana Alliluyeva defects to the United States.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: The Zapruder film of the assassination of John F. Kennedy is shown in motion to a national TV audience for the first time by Robert J. Groden and Dick Gregory.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Marcus Aurelius and L. Commodus (who changes his name to Lucius Verus) become joint emperors of Rome on the death of Antoninus Pius.
name: Marcus Aurelius

text: Napoleon Bonaparte captures Jaffa in Palestine and his troops proceed to kill more than 2,000 Albanian captives.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Alexander Graham Bell is granted a patent for an invention he calls the "telephone".
name: Alexander Graham Bell

text: Cold War: While addressing a convention of Evangelicals, U.S. President Ronald Reagan labels the Soviet Union an "evil empire".
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Scottish philosopher Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations, ushering in the classical period of political economy.
name: Adam Smith

text: Napoléon Bonaparte marries his first wife, Joséphine de Beauharnais.
name: Joséphine de Beauharnais

text: Giuseppe Verdi's third opera, Nabucco, receives its première performance in Milan; its success establishes Verdi as one of Italy's foremost opera composers.
name: Giuseppe Verdi

text: The first successful test of a telephone is made by Alexander Graham Bell.
name: Alexander Graham Bell

text: Mahatma Gandhi is arrested in India, tried for sedition, and sentenced to six years in prison, only to be released after nearly two years for an appendicitis operation.
name: Mahatma Gandhi

text: Fulgencio Batista leads a successful coup in Cuba.
name: Fulgencio Batista

text: The first performance of Rigoletto by Giuseppe Verdi takes place in Venice.
name: Giuseppe Verdi

text: Mikhail Gorbachev is elected to the position of General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, making Gorbachev the USSR's de facto, and last, head of state.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Ignatius of Loyola and Francis Xavier, founders of the Society of Jesus, are canonized by the Roman Catholic Church.
name: Francis Xavier

text: James II of England landed at Kinsale, starting the Williamite War in Ireland.
name: James II of England

text: Mahatma Gandhi begins the Salt March, a 200-mile (320 km) march to the sea to protest the British monopoly on salt in India.
name: Mahatma Gandhi

text: William Herschel discovers Uranus.
name: William Herschel

text: Cuban student revolutionaries storm the presidential palace in Havana in a failed attempt on the life of President Fulgencio Batista.
name: Fulgencio Batista

text: The Missionaries of Charity choose Sister Nirmala to succeed Mother Teresa as their leader.
name: Mother Teresa

text: Jack Ruby is convicted of killing Lee Harvey Oswald, the assassin who had shot and killed John F. Kennedy in the previous year.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: The body of U.S. President John F. Kennedy is moved to a permanent burial place at Arlington National Cemetery.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: King Charles II of England issues the Royal Declaration of Indulgence, granting limited religious freedom to all Christians.
name: Charles II of England

text: In an emotional speech in Newburgh, New York, George Washington asks his officers not to support the Newburgh Conspiracy. The plea is successful, and the threatened coup d'état never takes place.
name: George Washington

text: Tsar Nicholas II of Russia abdicates the Russian throne, ending the 304-year Romanov dynasty.
name: Nicholas II of Russia

text: President Lyndon B. Johnson, responding to the Selma crisis, tells U.S. Congress "We shall overcome" while advocating the Voting Rights Act.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Mikhail Gorbachev is elected as the first President of the Soviet Union.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Adolf Hitler orders Germany to rearm itself in violation of the Treaty of Versailles. Conscription is reintroduced to form the Wehrmacht.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Halabja chemical attack: The Kurdish town of Halabja in Iraq is attacked with a mix of poison gas and nerve agents on the orders of Saddam Hussein, killing 5,000 people and injuring about 10,000 people.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Commodus becomes sole emperor of the Roman Empire at the age of eighteen, following the death of his father, Marcus Aurelius.
name: Marcus Aurelius

text: American Revolution: The British Army evacuates Boston, ending the Siege of Boston, after George Washington and Henry Knox place artillery in positions overlooking the city.
name: George Washington

text: Golda Meir becomes the first female Prime Minister of Israel.
name: Golda Meir

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini meet at the Brenner Pass in the Alps and agree to form an alliance against France and the United Kingdom.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: Frank Nitti, the Chicago Outfit Boss after Al Capone, commits suicide at the Chicago Central Railyard.
name: Al Capone

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler issues his "Nero Decree" ordering all industries, military installations, shops, transportation facilities, and communications facilities in Germany to be destroyed.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Albert Einstein submits his paper, "The Foundation of the General Theory of Relativity", which establishes his general theory of relativity, to the journal Annalen der Physik.
name: Albert Einstein

text: The Arts Club of Chicago hosts the opening of Pablo Picasso's first United States showing, entitled Original Drawings by Pablo Picasso, becoming an early proponent of modern art in the United States.
name: Pablo Picasso

text: Reichsführer-SS Heinrich Himmler ordered the creation of Dachau concentration camp as Chief of Police of Munich and appointed Theodor Eicke as the camp commandant.
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: Journalist Henry Morton Stanley begins his trek to find the missionary and explorer David Livingstone.
name: David Livingstone

text: Charles Lindbergh is presented with the Medal of Honor for the first solo trans-Atlantic flight.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: Wehrmacht officer Rudolf von Gersdorff plots to assassinate Adolf Hitler by using a suicide bomb, but the plan falls through; von Gersdorff is able to defuse the bomb in time and avoid suspicion.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Cold War: American President Jimmy Carter announces a United States boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympics in Moscow to protest the Soviet-Afghan War.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: Pope John Paul II makes his first ever pontifical visit to Israel.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Ferdinand II of Aragon commissions Amerigo Vespucci chief navigator of the Spanish Empire.
name: Amerigo Vespucci

text: The United States Congress votes to override President Ronald Reagan's veto of the Civil Rights Restoration Act of 1987.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Waltham Abbey is surrendered to King Henry VIII of England; the last religious community to be closed during the Dissolution of the Monasteries.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: In Milan, Italy, Benito Mussolini founds his Fascist political movement.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: The Reichstag passes the Enabling Act of 1933, making Adolf Hitler dictator of Germany.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Strategic Defense Initiative: President Ronald Reagan makes his initial proposal to develop technology to intercept enemy missiles.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: King Richard I of England is wounded by a crossbow bolt while fighting in France, leading to his death on April 6.
name: Richard I of England

text: Tokugawa Ieyasu is granted the title of shōgun from Emperor Go-Yōzei, and establishes the Tokugawa shogunate in Edo, Japan.
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: The Province of Carolina is granted by charter to eight Lords Proprietor in reward for their assistance in restoring Charles II of England to the throne.
name: Charles II of England

text: Johann Sebastian Bach dedicated six concertos to Margrave Christian Ludwig of Brandenburg-Schwedt, now commonly called the Brandenburg Concertos, BWV 1046-1051.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: Robert Koch announces the discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis.
name: Robert Koch

text: Saturn's largest moon, Titan, is discovered by Christiaan Huygens.
name: Christiaan Huygens

text: Percy Bysshe Shelley is expelled from the University of Oxford for publishing the pamphlet The Necessity of Atheism.
name: Percy Bysshe Shelley

text: United States Customs seizes copies of Allen Ginsberg's poem "Howl" on obscenity grounds.
name: Allen Ginsberg

text: The first fully functional Space Shuttle orbiter, Columbia, is delivered to the John F. Kennedy Space Center to be prepared for its first launch.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Anwar al-Sadat, Menachem Begin and Jimmy Carter sign the Egypt-Israel peace treaty in Washington, D.C.
name: Menachem Begin

text: Texas Revolution: On the orders of General Antonio López de Santa Anna, the Mexican Army massacres 342 Texian Army POWs at Goliad, Texas.
name: Antonio López de Santa Anna

text: Spanish Civil War: Generalissimo Francisco Franco conquers Madrid after a three-year siege.
name: Francisco Franco

text: At the Diet of Porvoo, Finland's four Estates pledge allegiance to Alexander I of Russia, commencing the secession of the Grand Duchy of Finland from Sweden.
name: Alexander I of Russia

text: Delta Air Lines Flight 9877 crashes at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport, killing 19.
name: Louis Armstrong

text: U.S. President Ronald Reagan is shot in the chest outside a Washington, D.C., hotel by John Hinckley Jr.; three others are wounded in the same incident.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: The Long Parliament presents the Humble Petition and Advice offering Oliver Cromwell the British throne, which he eventually declines.
name: Oliver Cromwell

text: Rusalka by Antonín Dvořák premieres at the National Opera House in Prague.
name: Antonín Dvořák

text: The Vienna Concert Society rioted during a performance of modernist music by Arnold Schoenberg, Alban Berg, Alexander von Zemlinsky, and Anton von Webern, causing a premature end to the concert due to violence; this concert became known as the Skandalkonzert.
name: Arnold Schoenberg

text: American President Lyndon B. Johnson speaks to the nation of "Steps to Limit the War in Vietnam" in a television address. At the conclusion of his speech, he announces: "I shall not seek, and I will not accept, the nomination of my party for another term as your President."
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Adolf Hitler is sentenced to five years fortress confinement for his participation in the "Beer Hall Putsch" but spends only nine months in jail.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: The recently elected Nazis under Julius Streicher organize a one-day boycott of all Jewish-owned businesses in Germany, ushering in a series of anti-Semitic acts.
name: Julius Streicher

text: Spanish Civil War: Generalísimo Francisco Franco of the Spanish State announces the end of the Spanish Civil War, when the last of the Republican forces surrender.
name: Francisco Franco

text: Margaret Thatcher's new local government tax, the Community Charge (commonly known as the "poll tax"), is introduced in Scotland.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: Former President of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Slobodan Milošević surrenders to police special forces, to be tried on war crimes charges.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: Ludwig van Beethoven leads the premiere of his First Symphony in Vienna.
name: Ludwig van Beethoven

text: United States President Jimmy Carter signs the Crude Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev arrives in Havana, Cuba, to meet with Fidel Castro in an attempt to mend strained relations.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: American Old West: Robert Ford kills Jesse James.
name: Jesse James

text: The trial in the libel case brought by Oscar Wilde begins, eventually resulting in his imprisonment on charges of homosexuality.
name: Oscar Wilde

text: Joseph Stalin becomes the first General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Bruno Richard Hauptmann is executed for the kidnapping and death of Charles Augustus Lindbergh Jr., the infant son of pilot Charles Lindbergh.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: The American Civil Liberties Union announces it will defend Allen Ginsberg's book Howl against obscenity charges.
name: Allen Ginsberg

text: Georges Cuvier delivers the first paleontological lecture.
name: Georges Cuvier

text: American Civil War: A day after Union forces capture Richmond, Virginia, U.S. President Abraham Lincoln visits the Confederate capital.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Alexander II of Russia narrowly escapes an assassination attempt by Dmitry Karakozov in the city of Saint Petersburg.
name: Alexander II of Russia

text: The Schutzstaffel (SS) is founded under Adolf Hitler's Nazi Party in Germany.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: President Ronald Reagan calls for an international ban on chemical weapons.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: During the Battle on the Ice of Lake Peipus, Russian forces, led by Alexander Nevsky, rebuff an invasion attempt by the Teutonic Knights.
name: Alexander Nevsky

text: United States President George Washington exercises his authority to veto a bill, the first time this power is used in the United States.
name: George Washington

text: Spanish Civil War: Two days after the Nationalist army occupied the Catalan city of Lleida, dictator Francisco Franco decrees the abolition of the Generalitat (the autonomous government of Catalonia), the self-government granted by the Republic, and the official status of the Catalan language.
name: Francisco Franco

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler issues Fuhrer Directive No. 41 summarizing Case Blue, including the German Sixth Army's planned assault on Stalingrad.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Cold War: Yugoslav leader Josip Broz Tito signs an agreement with the Soviet Union to allow "temporary entry of Soviet troops into Yugoslav territory".
name: Josip Broz Tito

text: Cuban Revolution: Fidel Castro declares himself at war with Cuban President Fulgencio Batista.
name: Fulgencio Batista

text: The flag carrier airline of Greece for decades, Olympic Airways, is founded by Aristotle Onassis following the acquisition of "TAE - Greek National Airlines".
name: Aristotle Onassis

text: Francis Xavier leaves Lisbon on a mission to the Portuguese East Indies.
name: Francis Xavier

text: German composer Ludwig van Beethoven premieres his Third Symphony, at the Theater an der Wien in Vienna.
name: Ludwig van Beethoven

text: Violet Gibson attempts to assassinate Italian Prime Minister Benito Mussolini.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: Benito Mussolini declares an Italian protectorate over Albania and forces King Zog I into exile.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: Benito Mussolini invades Albania.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: Winston Churchill resigns as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom amid indications of failing health.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Development of the neutron bomb is canceled by President Jimmy Carter.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: Iraq War: U.S. troops capture Baghdad; Saddam Hussein's Ba'athist regime falls two days later.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Former Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is arrested for corruption by determination of Judge Sérgio Moro, from the "Car-Wash Operation". Lula stayed imprisoned for 580 days, after being released by the Brazilian Supreme Court.
name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva

text: Roger II of Sicily is excommunicated by Innocent II for supporting Anacletus II as pope for seven years, even though Roger had already publicly recognized Innocent's claim to the papacy.
name: Roger II of Sicily

text: Seventh Crusade: Ayyubids of Egypt capture King Louis IX of France in the Battle of Fariskur.
name: Louis IX of France

text: The distinguished soldier Septimius Severus is proclaimed emperor by the army in Illyricum.
name: Septimius Severus

text: Philip III of Spain issues the decree of the "Expulsion of the Moriscos".
name: Philip III of Spain

text: Vidkun Quisling seizes power in Norway.
name: Vidkun Quisling

text: Dietrich Bonhoeffer, Lutheran pastor and anti-Nazi dissident, is executed by the Nazi regime.
name: Dietrich Bonhoeffer

text: The Iraqi regime of Saddam Hussein kills philosopher Muhammad Baqir al-Sadr and his sister Bint al-Huda after three days of torture.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: On Easter Sunday, Pope Leo XIII authorizes the establishment of the Catholic University of America.
name: Pope Leo XIII

text: Mexican Revolution leader Emiliano Zapata is ambushed and shot dead by government forces in Morelos.
name: Emiliano Zapata

text: The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald is first published in New York City, by Charles Scribner's Sons.
name: F. Scott Fitzgerald

text: The Russian city of Tsaritsyn was renamed Stalingrad to honor the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, Soviet Communist Party General Secretary, who had guided the defense of Tsaritsyn during the Russian Civil War in 1920.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Premiere of Johann Sebastian Bach's St Matthew Passion BWV 244b at St. Thomas Church in Leipzig, Electorate of Saxony (now Germany).
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: The Treaty of Fontainebleau ends the War of the Sixth Coalition against Napoleon Bonaparte, and forces him to abdicate unconditionally for the first time.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Stresa Front: opening of the conference between the British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald, the Italian Prime Minister Benito Mussolini and the French Minister for Foreign Affairs Pierre Laval to condemn the German violations of the Treaty of Versailles.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: The trial of Adolf Eichmann begins in Jerusalem.
name: Adolf Eichmann

text: Pope John XXIII issues Pacem in terris, the first encyclical addressed to all Christians instead of only Catholics, and which described the conditions for world peace in human terms.
name: Pope John XXIII

text: US President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act of 1968, prohibiting discrimination in the sale, rental, and financing of housing.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: The London Agreement is secretly signed between Israeli Foreign Affairs Minister Shimon Peres and King Hussein of Jordan.
name: Shimon Peres

text: War of the First Coalition: Napoleon Bonaparte wins his first victory as an army commander at the Battle of Montenotte, splitting the Austrian and Piedmontese armies away from each other, and marking the beginning of the Piedmontese surrender in the war.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: George Frideric Handel's oratorio Messiah makes its world premiere in Dublin, Ireland.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: The Jefferson Memorial is dedicated in Washington, D.C., on the 200th anniversary of President Thomas Jefferson's birth.
name: Thomas Jefferson

text: The United States Treasury Department reintroduces the two-dollar bill as a Federal Reserve Note on Thomas Jefferson's 233rd birthday as part of the United States Bicentennial celebration.
name: Thomas Jefferson

text: The Society for the Relief of Free Negroes Unlawfully Held in Bondage, the first abolition society in North America, is organized in Philadelphia by Benjamin Franklin and Benjamin Rush.
name: Benjamin Franklin

text: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln is shot in Ford's Theatre by John Wilkes Booth; Lincoln dies the following day.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Serse, an Italian opera by George Frideric Handel, receives its premiere performance in London, England.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: President Abraham Lincoln  calls for 75,000 militiamen to quell the insurrection that soon became the American Civil War.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: President Abraham Lincoln dies after being shot the previous evening by actor John Wilkes Booth. Three hours later, Vice President Andrew Johnson is sworn in as president.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Russian Revolution: Vladimir Lenin returns to Petrograd, Russia, from exile in Switzerland.
name: Vladimir Lenin

text: In a nationally broadcast speech, Cuban leader Fidel Castro declares that he is a Marxist-Leninist and that Cuba is going to adopt Communism.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Trial of Martin Luther over his teachings begins during the assembly of the Diet of Worms. Initially intimidated, he asks for time to reflect before answering and is given a stay of one day.
name: Martin Luther

text: Bay of Pigs Invasion: A group of Cuban exiles financed and trained by the CIA lands at the Bay of Pigs in Cuba with the aim of ousting Fidel Castro.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Communist Party of Czechoslovakia chairman Alexander Dubček is deposed.
name: Alexander Dubček

text: Trial of Martin Luther begins its second day during the assembly of the Diet of Worms. He refuses to recant his teachings despite the risk of excommunication.
name: Martin Luther

text: World War II: Operation Vengeance, Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto is killed when his aircraft is shot down by U.S. fighters over Bougainville Island.
name: Isoroku Yamamoto

text: Gamal Abdel Nasser seizes power in Egypt.
name: Gamal Abdel Nasser

text: Captain James Cook, still holding the rank of lieutenant, sights the eastern coast of what is now Australia.
name: James Cook

text: Marie Antoinette marries Louis XVI in a proxy wedding.
name: Marie Antoinette

text: Charles Manson is sentenced to death (later commuted to life imprisonment) for conspiracy in the Tate-LaBianca murders.
name: Charles Manson

text: Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger is elected to the papacy and becomes Pope Benedict XVI.
name: Pope Benedict XVI

text: Fidel Castro resigns as First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba after holding the title since July 1961.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Oliver Cromwell dissolves England's Rump Parliament.
name: Oliver Cromwell

text: George Washington arrives at Grays Ferry, Philadelphia, while en route to Manhattan for his inauguration.
name: George Washington

text: Louis Pasteur and Claude Bernard complete the experiment disproving the theory of spontaneous generation.
name: Louis Pasteur

text: Astronomer Angelo Secchi demonstrates the Secchi disk, which measures water clarity, aboard Pope Pius IX's yacht, the L'Immaculata Concezion.
name: Pope Pius IX

text: Pope Leo XIII publishes the encyclical Humanum genus, condemning Freemasonry.
name: Pope Leo XIII

text: Pierre and Marie Curie refine radium chloride.
name: Marie Curie

text: Manfred von Richthofen, a.k.a. The Red Baron, shoots down his 79th and 80th victims, his final victories before his death the following day.
name: Manfred von Richthofen

text: World War II: Führerbunker: On his 56th birthday Adolf Hitler makes his last trip to the surface to award Iron Crosses to boy soldiers of the Hitler Youth.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: John Adams sworn in as first US Vice President (nine days before George Washington).
name: George Washington

text: George Washington's reception at Trenton is hosted by the Ladies of Trenton as he journeys to New York City for his first inauguration.
name: George Washington

text: War of the First Coalition: In the climax of the Montenotte Campaign, Napoleon Bonaparte decisively defeats the army of Piedmont at the Battle of Mondovi, leading to Piedmont's surrender a week later and decisively turning the Italian campaign in France's favor.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Texas Revolution: The Battle of San Jacinto: Republic of Texas forces under Sam Houston defeat troops under Mexican General Antonio López de Santa Anna.
name: Antonio López de Santa Anna

text: World War I: German fighter ace Manfred von Richthofen, better known as "The Red Baron", is shot down and killed over Vaux-sur-Somme in France.
name: Manfred von Richthofen

text: Texas Revolution: A day after the Battle of San Jacinto, forces under Texas General Sam Houston identify Mexican General Antonio López de Santa Anna among the captives of the battle when some of his fellow soldiers mistakenly give away his identity.
name: Antonio López de Santa Anna

text: King Charles II of England, Scotland and Ireland is crowned in Westminster Abbey.
name: Charles II of England

text: Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of his cantata Du Hirte Israel, höre, BWV 104, illustrating the topic of the Good Shepherd in pastoral music.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler's designated successor, Hermann Göring, sends him a telegram asking permission to take leadership of Nazi Germany. Martin Bormann and Joseph Goebbels advise Göring that the telegram is treasonous.
name: Hermann Göring

text: French revolutionary Jean-Paul Marat is acquitted by the Revolutionary Tribunal of charges brought by the Girondin in Paris.
name: Jean-Paul Marat

text: American sharpshooter Annie Oakley is hired by Nate Salsbury to be a part of Buffalo Bill's Wild West.
name: Buffalo Bill

text: Winston Churchill is knighted by Queen Elizabeth II.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger is inaugurated as the 265th Pope of the Catholic Church taking the name Pope Benedict XVI.
name: Pope Benedict XVI

text: Cold War: American schoolgirl Samantha Smith is invited to visit the Soviet Union by its leader Yuri Andropov after he read her letter in which she expressed fears about nuclear war.
name: Yuri Andropov

text: The Pazzi family attack on Lorenzo de' Medici in order to displace the ruling Medici family kills his brother Giuliano during High Mass in Florence Cathedral.
name: Lorenzo de' Medici

text: Playwright William Shakespeare is baptized in Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, England (date of birth is unknown).
name: William Shakespeare

text: Napoleon Bonaparte signs a general amnesty to allow all but about one thousand of the most notorious émigrés of the French Revolution to return to France.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Union cavalry troopers corner and shoot dead John Wilkes Booth, assassin of President Abraham Lincoln, in Virginia.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Paul von Hindenburg defeats Wilhelm Marx in the second round of the German presidential election to become the first directly elected head of state of the Weimar Republic.
name: Paul von Hindenburg

text: The Gestapo, the official secret police force of Nazi Germany, is established by Hermann Göring.
name: Hermann Göring

text: Blind and impoverished, John Milton sells Paradise Lost to a printer for £10, so that it could be entered into the Stationers' Register.
name: John Milton

text: American President Abraham Lincoln suspends the writ of habeas corpus.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: World War II: Benito Mussolini is arrested by Italian partisans in Dongo, while attempting escape disguised as a German soldier.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: The U.S. Department of Justice bars Austrian President Kurt Waldheim (and his wife, Elisabeth, who had also been a Nazi) from entering the US, charging that he had aided in the deportations and executions of thousands of Jews and others as a German Army officer during World War II.
name: Kurt Waldheim

text: The Armistice of Cherasco is signed by Napoleon Bonaparte and Vittorio Amedeo III, King of Sardinia, expanding French territory along the Mediterranean coast.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci are shot dead by Walter Audisio, a member of the Italian resistance movement.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: The West German news magazine Stern begins publishing excerpts from the purported diaries of Adolf Hitler, later revealed to be forgeries.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: James Cook arrives in Australia at Botany Bay, which he names.
name: James Cook

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler marries his longtime partner Eva Braun in a Berlin bunker and designates Admiral Karl Dönitz as his successor.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Henry IV of France issues the Edict of Nantes, allowing freedom of religion to the Huguenots.
name: Henry IV of France

text: On the balcony of Federal Hall on Wall Street in New York City, George Washington takes the oath of office to become the first President of the United States.
name: George Washington

text: Albert Einstein completes his doctoral thesis at the University of Zurich.
name: Albert Einstein

text: World War II: Führerbunker: Adolf Hitler and Eva Braun commit suicide after being married for less than 40 hours. Soviet soldiers raise the Victory Banner over the Reichstag building.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: World War II: German radio broadcasts news of Adolf Hitler's death, falsely stating that he has "fallen at his command post in the Reich Chancellery fighting to the last breath against Bolshevism and for Germany". The Soviet flag is raised over the Reich Chancellery, by order of Stalin.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: The Prime Minister of Cuba, Fidel Castro, proclaims Cuba a socialist nation and abolishes elections.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Pope John Paul II is beatified by his successor, Pope Benedict XVI.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: King Richard I of England gives Portsmouth its first royal charter.
name: Richard I of England

text: King Charles II of England grants a permanent charter to the Hudson's Bay Company to open up the fur trade in North America.
name: Charles II of England

text: Erich Honecker becomes First Secretary of the Socialist Unity Party of Germany, remaining in power until 1989.
name: Erich Honecker

text: Margaret Thatcher wins the United Kingdom general election. The following day, she becomes the first female British Prime Minister.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: In the papal bull Inter caetera, Pope Alexander VI divides the New World between Spain and Portugal along the Line of Demarcation.
name: Pope Alexander VI

text: Having been incarcerated at the Cook County Jail since his sentencing on October 24, 1931, mobster Al Capone is transferred to the federal penitentiary in Atlanta after the U.S. Supreme Court denies his appeal for conviction of tax evasion.
name: Al Capone

text: Margaret Thatcher becomes the first female Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: Kublai Khan becomes ruler of the Mongol Empire.
name: Kublai Khan

text: King Charles I of England dissolves the Short Parliament.
name: Charles I of England

text: Ronald Reagan visits the military cemetery at Bitburg and the site of the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, where he makes a speech.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Francis Xavier reaches Old Goa, the capital of Portuguese India at the time.
name: Francis Xavier

text: John Steinbeck is awarded the Pulitzer Prize for his novel The Grapes of Wrath.
name: John Steinbeck

text: One hundred and three Korean Martyrs are canonized by Pope John Paul II in Seoul.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: During a trip to Syria, Pope John Paul II becomes the first pope to enter a mosque.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: World premiere of Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony in Vienna, Austria. The performance is conducted by Michael Umlauf under the composer's supervision.
name: Ludwig van Beethoven

text: Spanish Civil War: The German Condor Legion, equipped with Heinkel He 51 biplanes, arrives in Spain to assist Francisco Franco's forces.
name: Francisco Franco

text: World War II: The Norway Debate in the British House of Commons begins, and leads to the replacement of Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain with Winston Churchill three days later.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Pope John Paul II travels to Romania, becoming the first pope to visit a predominantly Eastern Orthodox country since the Great Schism in 1054.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Vladimir Putin is inaugurated as president of Russia.
name: Vladimir Putin

text: Treaty of Brétigny drafted between King Edward III of England and King John II of France (the Good).
name: Edward III of England

text: King Louis XVI of France attempts to impose the reforms of Étienne Charles de Loménie de Brienne by abolishing the parlements.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: Branded a traitor during the Reign of Terror, French chemist Antoine Lavoisier, who was also a tax collector with the Ferme générale, is tried, convicted and guillotined in one day in Paris.
name: Antoine Lavoisier

text: King Victor Emmanuel III of Italy abdicates and is succeeded by Umberto II.
name: Victor Emmanuel III of Italy

text: Robert Schuman presents the "Schuman Declaration", considered by some to be the beginning of the creation of what is now the European Union.
name: Robert Schuman

text: Amerigo Vespucci allegedly leaves Cádiz for his first voyage to the New World.
name: Amerigo Vespucci

text: Jacques Cartier visits Newfoundland.
name: Jacques Cartier

text: Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette become King and Queen of France.
name: Marie Antoinette

text: World War II: Winston Churchill is appointed Prime Minister of the United Kingdom following the resignation of Neville Chamberlain. On the same day, Germany invades France, The Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg. Meanwhile, the United Kingdom occupies Iceland.
name: Winston Churchill

text: World War II: Rudolf Hess parachutes into Scotland to try to negotiate a peace deal between the United Kingdom and Nazi Germany.
name: Rudolf Hess

text: Louis IX of France and James I of Aragon sign the Treaty of Corbeil, renouncing claims of feudal overlordship in one another's territories and separating the House of Barcelona from the politics of France.
name: Louis IX of France

text: Richard I of England marries Berengaria of Navarre in Cyprus; she is crowned Queen consort of England the same day.
name: Richard I of England

text: Pope Alexander VI excommunicates Girolamo Savonarola.
name: Girolamo Savonarola

text: French Wars of Religion: Henry III of France flees Paris after Henry I, Duke of Guise, enters the city and a spontaneous uprising occurs.
name: Henry III of France

text: War of the First Coalition: Napoleon Bonaparte conquers Venice.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Ten weeks after his abduction, Charles Jr., the infant son of Charles Lindbergh, is found dead near Hopewell, New Jersey, just a few miles from the Lindberghs' home.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: During a procession outside the shrine of the Virgin Mary in Fátima, Portugal, security guards overpower Juan María Fernández y Krohn before he can attack Pope John Paul II with a bayonet.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Former US President Jimmy Carter arrives in Cuba for a five-day visit with Fidel Castro, becoming the first President of the United States, in or out of office, to visit the island since the Cuban Revolution.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Amerigo Vespucci, this time under Portuguese flag, set sail for western lands.
name: Amerigo Vespucci

text: World War II: Germany's conquest of France begins, as the German army crosses the Meuse. Winston Churchill makes his "blood, toil, tears, and sweat" speech to the House of Commons.
name: Winston Churchill

text: An F3 tornado hits Kalamazoo County, Michigan. President Jimmy Carter declares it a federal disaster area.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: Mehmet Ali Ağca attempts to assassinate Pope John Paul II in St. Peter's Square in Rome. The Pope is rushed to the Agostino Gemelli University Polyclinic to undergo emergency surgery and survives.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Battle of Lewes: Henry III of England is captured and forced to sign the Mise of Lewes, making Simon de Montfort the effective ruler of England.
name: Henry III of England

text: Henry IV of France is assassinated by Catholic zealot François Ravaillac, and Louis XIII ascends the throne.
name: Henry IV of France

text: Edward Jenner administers the first smallpox inoculation.
name: Edward Jenner

text: French Revolution: Maximilien Robespierre proposes the Self-denying Ordinance.
name: Maximilien Robespierre

text: Pope Leo XIII defends workers' rights and property rights in the encyclical Rerum novarum, the beginning of modern Catholic social teaching.
name: Pope Leo XIII

text: Joseph Stalin dissolves the Comintern (or Third International).
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Sir Thomas More resigns as Lord Chancellor of England.
name: Thomas More

text: The 14-year-old Marie Antoinette marries 15-year-old Louis-Auguste, who later becomes king of France.
name: Marie Antoinette

text: Nikola Tesla delivers a lecture describing the equipment which will allow efficient generation and use of alternating currents to transmit electric power over long distances.
name: Nikola Tesla

text: In Rome, Pope Benedict XV canonizes Joan of Arc.
name: Pope Benedict XV

text: Josip Broz Tito is elected president for life of Yugoslavia.
name: Josip Broz Tito

text: Mobutu Sese Seko, the President of Zaire, flees the country.
name: Mobutu Sese Seko

text: Muhammad Ali becomes Wāli of Egypt.
name: Muhammad Ali

text: Vidkun Quisling and Johan Bernhard Hjort form Nasjonal Samling — the national-socialist party of Norway.
name: Vidkun Quisling

text: Six-Day War: President Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt demands dismantling of the peace-keeping UN Emergency Force in Egypt.
name: Gamal Abdel Nasser

text: The future Henry II of England marries Eleanor of Aquitaine. He would become king two years later, after the death of his cousin once removed King Stephen of England.
name: Henry II of England

text: Playwright Thomas Kyd's accusations of heresy lead to an arrest warrant for Christopher Marlowe.
name: Christopher Marlowe

text: Napoleon Bonaparte is proclaimed Emperor of the French by the French Senate.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: United States presidential election: Abraham Lincoln wins the Republican Party presidential nomination over William H. Seward, who later becomes the United States Secretary of State.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Likud party wins the 1977 Israeli legislative election, with Menachem Begin, its founder, as the sixth Prime Minister of Israel.
name: Menachem Begin

text: Catherine of Aragon is married by proxy to Arthur, Prince of Wales. Catherine is 13 and Arthur is 12.
name: Catherine of Aragon

text: French explorer Jacques Cartier sets sail on his second voyage to North America with three ships, 110 men, and Chief Donnacona's two sons (whom Cartier had kidnapped during his first voyage).
name: Jacques Cartier

text: Anne Boleyn, the second wife of Henry VIII of England, is beheaded for adultery, treason, and incest.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Napoleon Bonaparte founds the Legion of Honour.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Buffalo Bill's first Buffalo Bill's Wild West opens in Omaha, Nebraska.
name: Buffalo Bill

text: Winston Churchill's second wartime address to the U.S. Congress
name: Winston Churchill

text: A birthday salute to U.S. President John F. Kennedy takes place at Madison Square Garden, New York City. The highlight is Marilyn Monroe's rendition of "Happy Birthday".
name: John F. Kennedy

text: The Firearm Owners Protection Act is signed into law by U.S. President Ronald Reagan.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of his cantata for Pentecost, Erschallet, ihr Lieder, BWV 172, at the chapel of Schloss Weimar.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: By the Law of 20 May 1802, Napoleon Bonaparte reinstates slavery in the French colonies, revoking its abolition in the French Revolution.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Napoleon Bonaparte leads his French troops into the Battle of Bautzen in Saxony, Germany, against the combined armies of Russia and Prussia. The battle ends the next day with a French victory.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln signs the Homestead Act into law, opening eighty-four million acres (340,000 km2) of public land to settlers.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Charles Lindbergh takes off for Paris from Roosevelt Field in Long Island, N.Y., aboard the Spirit of St. Louis on the first nonstop solo flight across the Atlantic Ocean, landing .mw-parser-output .frac{white-space:nowrap}.mw-parser-output .frac .num,.mw-parser-output .frac .den{font-size:80%;line-height:0;vertical-align:super}.mw-parser-output .frac .den{vertical-align:sub}.mw-parser-output .sr-only{border:0;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);clip-path:polygon(0px 0px,0px 0px,0px 0px);height:1px;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px}33+1⁄2 hours later.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: The end of the Siege of Acre (1799): Napoleon Bonaparte abandons his siege of the Ottoman city of Acre after two months. This was the turning point of Bonaparte's Egyptian campaign and one of the first major defeats he suffered in his military career.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Charles Lindbergh touches down at Le Bourget Field in Paris, completing the world's first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic Ocean.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: Margaret Thatcher holds her controversial Sermon on the Mound before the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: After 30 seasons Johnny Carson hosted his penultimate episode and last featuring guests (Robin Williams and Bette Midler) of The Tonight Show.
name: Robin Williams

text: King John of England and King Philip II of France sign the Treaty of Le Goulet.
name: Philip II of France

text: Future U.S. President Abraham Lincoln is issued a patent for an invention to lift boats, making him the only U.S. president to ever hold a patent.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Joseph Stalin disbands the Comintern.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson launches his Great Society program.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Girolamo Savonarola is burned at the stake in Florence, Italy.
name: Girolamo Savonarola

text: The marriage of King Henry VIII to Catherine of Aragon is declared null and void.
name: Catherine of Aragon

text: World War II: Heinrich Himmler, head of the Schutzstaffel, commits suicide while in Allied custody.
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: World War II: Germany's Flensburg Government under Karl Dönitz is dissolved when its members are arrested by British forces.
name: Karl Dönitz

text: South American independence leader Simón Bolívar enters Mérida, leading the invasion of Venezuela, and is proclaimed El Libertador ("The Liberator").
name: Simón Bolívar

text: Acting on the orders of Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, NKVD agent Iosif Grigulevich orchestrates an unsuccessful assassination attempt on exiled Russian revolutionary Leon Trotsky in Coyoacán, Mexico.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Belle de Jour, directed by Luis Buñuel, is released.
name: Luis Buñuel

text: The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague, Netherlands indicts Slobodan Milošević and four others for war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Kosovo.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: Henry the Navigator is appointed governor of the Order of Christ.
name: Henry the Navigator

text: The Diet of Worms ends when Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, issues the Edict of Worms, declaring Martin Luther an outlaw.
name: Martin Luther

text: Playwright, poet and novelist Oscar Wilde is convicted of "committing acts of gross indecency with other male persons" and sentenced to serve two years in prison.
name: Oscar Wilde

text: Apollo program: U.S. President John F. Kennedy announces, before a special joint session of the U.S. Congress, his goal to initiate a project to put a "man on the Moon" before the end of the decade.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Geneva expels John Calvin and his followers from the city. Calvin lives in exile in Strasbourg for the next three years.
name: John Calvin

text: Giuseppe Garibaldi begins the Siege of Palermo, part of the wars of Italian unification.
name: Giuseppe Garibaldi

text: Pope Benedict XV promulgates the 1917 Code of Canon Law, the first comprehensive codification of Catholic canon law in the legal history of the Catholic Church.
name: Pope Benedict XV

text: World War II: In Operation Anthropoid, Reinhard Heydrich is fatally wounded in Prague; he dies of his injuries eight days later.
name: Reinhard Heydrich

text: The U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS John F. Kennedy is launched by Jacqueline Kennedy and her daughter Caroline.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: The Archbishop of Canterbury, Thomas Cranmer, declares the marriage of King Henry VIII of England to Anne Boleyn valid.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: French and Indian War: In the first engagement of the war, Virginia militia under the 22-year-old Lieutenant colonel George Washington defeat a French reconnaissance party in the Battle of Jumonville Glen in what is now Fayette County in southwestern Pennsylvania.
name: George Washington

text: Alan Turing submits On Computable Numbers for publication.
name: Alan Turing

text: Cuban Revolution: Fidel Castro's 26th of July Movement, heavily reinforced by Frank Pais Militia, overwhelm an army post in El Uvero.
name: Fidel Castro

text: The Iraqi Governing Council chooses Ayad Allawi, a longtime anti-Saddam Hussein exile, as prime minister of Iraq's interim government.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: The Coronation of Charles X of France takes place in Reims Cathedral, the last ever coronation of a French monarch.
name: Charles X of France

text: Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico arrives in Mexico for the first time.
name: Maximilian I of Mexico

text: Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity is tested (later confirmed) by Arthur Eddington and Andrew Claude de la Cherois Crommelin.
name: Albert Einstein

text: Michele Schirru, a citizen of the United States, is executed by a Royal Italian Army firing squad for intent to kill Benito Mussolini.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: Pope John Paul II becomes the first pontiff to visit Canterbury Cathedral.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: U.S. President Ronald Reagan begins his first visit to the Soviet Union when he arrives in Moscow for a superpower summit with the Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: King Henry VIII of England marries Jane Seymour, a lady-in-waiting to his first two wives.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: From this date all honors granted by Charles I of England are retroactively annulled by Parliament.
name: Charles I of England

text: Johann Sebastian Bach assumed the office of Thomaskantor in Leipzig, presenting his first new cantata, Die Elenden sollen essen, BWV 75, in the St. Nicholas Church on the first Sunday after Trinity.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: War of the First Coalition: In the Battle of Borghetto, Napoleon Bonaparte manages to cross the Mincio River against the Austrian army. This crossing forces the Austrians to abandon Lombardy and retreat to the Tyrol, leaving the fortress of Mantua as the sole remaining stronghold in Northern Italy.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: In Dover, England, Charles II of England and Louis XIV of France sign the Secret Treaty of Dover, which will force England into the Third Anglo-Dutch War.
name: Charles II of England

text: War of 1812: U.S. President James Madison asks the Congress to declare war on the United Kingdom.
name: James Madison

text: Charles Baudelaire's Les Fleurs du mal is published.
name: Charles Baudelaire

text: BOAC Flight 777 is shot down over the Bay of Biscay by German Junkers Ju 88s, killing British actor Leslie Howard and leading to speculation that it was actually an attempt to kill British Prime Minister Winston Churchill.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Adolf Eichmann, former SS officer in Nazi Germany, is hanged in Israel for having committed crimes against humanity, war crimes, and other offenses.
name: Adolf Eichmann

text: Cold War: George H. W. Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev sign a treaty to end chemical weapon production.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: French Revolution: François Hanriot, leader of the Parisian National Guard, arrests 22 Girondists selected by Jean-Paul Marat, setting the stage for the Reign of Terror.
name: Jean-Paul Marat

text: Guglielmo Marconi applies for a patent for his wireless telegraph.
name: Guglielmo Marconi

text: Pope John Paul II starts his first official visit to his native Poland, becoming the first Pope to visit a Communist country.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Pope Alexander VII appoints François de Laval vicar apostolic in New France.
name: Pope Alexander VII

text: James Stuart, Duke of York (later to become King James II of England), defeats the Dutch fleet off the coast of Lowestoft.
name: James II of England

text: Franz Rademacher proposes plans to make Madagascar the "Jewish homeland", an idea that had first been considered by 19th century journalist Theodor Herzl.
name: Theodor Herzl

text: Siege of Osaka: Forces under Tokugawa Ieyasu take Osaka Castle in Japan.
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: Leon Trotsky bans the Planned Fourth Regional Congress of Peasants, Workers and Insurgents.
name: Leon Trotsky

text: World War II: The Dunkirk evacuation ends: the British Armed Forces completes evacuation of 338,000 troops from Dunkirk in France. To rally the morale of the country, Winston Churchill delivers, only to the House of Commons, his famous "We shall fight on the beaches" speech.
name: Winston Churchill

text: World War II: Gustaf Mannerheim, the Commander-in-Chief of the Finnish Army, is granted the title of Marshal of Finland by the government on his 75th birthday. On the same day, Adolf Hitler arrives in Finland for a surprise visit to meet Mannerheim.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Movement of 15 Khordad: Protests against the arrest of Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini by the Shah of Iran, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. In several cities, masses of angry demonstrators are confronted by tanks and paratroopers.
name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi

text: King Richard I of England arrives in Acre, beginning the Third Crusade.
name: Richard I of England

text: James Madison introduces twelve proposed amendments to the United States Constitution in Congress.
name: James Madison

text: Maximilien Robespierre inaugurates the French Revolution's new state religion, the Cult of the Supreme Being, with large organized festivals all across France.
name: Maximilien Robespierre

text: Jacques Cartier is the first European to describe and map the Saint Lawrence River.
name: Jacques Cartier

text: A Chicago Tribune reporter, Jake Lingle, is killed during rush hour at the Illinois Central train station by Leo Vincent Brothers, allegedly over a $100,000 gambling debt owed to Al Capone.
name: Al Capone

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson declares a national day of mourning following the assassination of Senator Robert F. Kennedy.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Council of Trent: Pope Paul III sends out letters to his bishops, delaying the Council due to war and the difficulty bishops had traveling to Venice.
name: Pope Paul III
