text: World War II: The Lidice massacre is perpetrated as a reprisal for the assassination of Obergruppenführer Reinhard Heydrich.
name: Reinhard Heydrich

text: The Equal Pay Act of 1963, aimed at abolishing wage disparity based on sex, was signed into law by John F. Kennedy as part of his New Frontier Program.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Kosovo War: NATO suspends its airstrikes after Slobodan Milošević agrees to withdraw Serbian forces from Kosovo.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: Pope John Paul II canonizes Lebanon's first female saint, Saint Rafqa.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Marcomannic Wars: The Roman army in Moravia is encircled by the Quadi, who have broken the peace treaty (171). In a violent thunderstorm emperor Marcus Aurelius defeats and subdues them in the so-called "miracle of the rain".
name: Marcus Aurelius

text: Henry VIII of England marries Catherine of Aragon.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Johann Sebastian Bach leads his cantata O Ewigkeit, du Donnerwort (O eternity, you word of thunder), BWV 20, on the first Sunday after Trinity, beginning his second cycle, the chorale cantata cycle.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: British explorer Captain James Cook runs aground on the Great Barrier Reef.
name: James Cook

text: The Continental Congress appoints Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Roger Sherman, and Robert R. Livingston to the Committee of Five to draft a declaration of independence.
name: Benjamin Franklin

text: Great Purge: The Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin executes eight army leaders.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: John F. Kennedy addresses Americans from the Oval Office proposing the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which would revolutionize American society by guaranteeing equal access to public facilities, ending segregation in education, and guaranteeing federal protection for voting rights.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: At the instigation of Louis IX of France, an inter-faith debate, known as the Disputation of Paris, starts between a Christian monk and four rabbis.
name: Louis IX of France

text: The city of Helsinki, Finland (belonging to Sweden at the time) is founded by King Gustav I of Sweden.
name: Gustav I of Sweden

text: World War II: Thirteen thousand British and French troops surrender to Major General Erwin Rommel at Saint-Valery-en-Caux.
name: Erwin Rommel

text: Anne Frank receives a diary for her thirteenth birthday.
name: Anne Frank

text: Pope Pius XII canonises Dominic Savio, who was 14 years old at the time of his death, as a saint, making him at the time the youngest unmartyred saint in the Roman Catholic Church. In 2017, Francisco and Jacinta Marto, aged ten and nine at the time of their deaths, are declared as saints.
name: Pope Pius XII

text: The film Cleopatra, starring Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, is released in US theaters. It was the most expensive film made at the time.
name: Elizabeth Taylor

text: Cold War: At the Brandenburg Gate, U.S. President Ronald Reagan publicly challenges Mikhail Gorbachev to tear down the Berlin Wall.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Ibn Battuta begins his travels, leaving his home in Tangiers to travel to Mecca (gone 24 years).
name: Ibn Battuta

text: Martin Luther marries Katharina von Bora, against the celibacy rule decreed by the Roman Catholic Church for priests and nuns.
name: Martin Luther

text: King Charles I of England marries Catholic princess Henrietta Maria of France and Navarre, at Canterbury.
name: Charles I of England

text: Twentieth opera of Giuseppe Verdi, Les vêpres siciliennes ("The Sicilian Vespers"), is premiered in Paris.
name: Giuseppe Verdi

text: Aviator Charles Lindbergh receives a ticker tape parade up 5th Avenue in New York City.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson nominates Solicitor-General Thurgood Marshall to become the first black justice on the U.S. Supreme Court.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Italy pardons Mehmet Ali Ağca, the Turkish gunman who tried to kill Pope John Paul II in 1981.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: The jury acquits pop singer Michael Jackson of his charges for allegedly sexually molesting a child in 1993.
name: Michael Jackson

text: Kublai Khan defeats the force of Nayan and other traditionalist Borjigin princes in East Mongolia and Manchuria.
name: Kublai Khan

text: King William III of England (William of Orange) lands in Ireland to confront the former King James II.
name: William III of England

text: The French Army of First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte defeats the Austrians at the Battle of Marengo in Northern Italy and re-conquers Italy.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Charles Babbage proposes a difference engine in a paper to the Royal Astronomical Society.
name: Charles Babbage

text: Pope Leo X threatens to excommunicate Martin Luther in Exsurge Domine.
name: Martin Luther

text: Benjamin Franklin proves that lightning is electricity (traditional date, the exact date is unknown).
name: Benjamin Franklin

text: Joseph Bonaparte becomes King of Spain.
name: Joseph Bonaparte

text: Charles Manson goes on trial for the Sharon Tate murders.
name: Charles Manson

text: After the death of dictator Francisco Franco in 1975, the first democratic elections take place in Spain.
name: Francisco Franco

text: The Papal conclave of 1846 elects Pope Pius IX, beginning the longest reign in the history of the papacy.
name: Pope Pius IX

text: Abraham Lincoln delivers his House Divided speech in Springfield, Illinois.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Roald Amundsen leaves Oslo, Norway, to commence the first east-west navigation of the Northwest Passage.
name: Roald Amundsen

text: US President Ronald Reagan awards the Congressional Gold Medal to Ken Taylor, Canada's former ambassador to Iran, for helping six Americans escape from Iran during the hostage crisis of 1979-81; he is the first foreign citizen bestowed the honor.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Battle of Civitate: Three thousand Norman horsemen of Count Humphrey rout the troops of Pope Leo IX.
name: Pope Leo IX

text: The United States declaration of war upon the United Kingdom is signed by President James Madison, beginning the War of 1812.
name: James Madison

text: Napoleonic Wars: The Battle of Waterloo results in the defeat of Napoleon Bonaparte by the Duke of Wellington and Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher forcing him to abdicate the throne of France for the second and last time.
name: Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher

text: Charles Darwin receives a paper from Alfred Russel Wallace that includes nearly identical conclusions about evolution as Darwin's own, prompting Darwin to publish his theory.
name: Alfred Russel Wallace

text: The "Finest Hour" speech is delivered by Winston Churchill.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Benito Mussolini, at the time a radical Socialist, is arrested by Bern police for advocating a violent general strike.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: Pope John Paul II canonizes 117 Vietnamese Martyrs.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Alexander Graham Bell installs the world's first commercial telephone service in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada.
name: Alexander Graham Bell

text: The United States Secretary of State approves the transfer of Wernher von Braun and his team of Nazi rocket scientists to the U.S. under Operation Paperclip.
name: Wernher von Braun

text: Sengoku period: Oda Nobunaga, the most powerful of the Japanese daimyōs, is forced to commit suicide by his own general Akechi Mitsuhide.
name: Oda Nobunaga

text: King Louis XVI of France and his immediate family begin the Flight to Varennes during the French Revolution.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: Peninsular War: Wellington defeats Joseph Bonaparte at the Battle of Vitoria.
name: Joseph Bonaparte

text: Cardinal Giovanni Battista Montini is elected as Pope Paul VI.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: The original production of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical, Evita, based on the life of Eva Perón, opens at the Prince Edward Theatre, London.
name: Eva Perón

text: John Hinckley is found not guilty by reason of insanity for the attempted assassination of U.S. President Ronald Reagan.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: The Holy Office in Rome forces Galileo Galilei to recant his view that the Sun, not the Earth, is the center of the Universe in the form he presented it in, after heated controversy.
name: Galileo Galilei

text: World War II: Erwin Rommel is promoted to Field Marshal after the Axis capture of Tobruk.
name: Erwin Rommel

text: Henry VIII of England and Francis I of France sign the "Treaty of Closer Amity With France" (also known as the Pommeraye treaty), pledging mutual aid against Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: The International Olympic Committee is founded at the Sorbonne in Paris, at the initiative of Baron Pierre de Coubertin.
name: Pierre de Coubertin

text: Adolf Hitler goes on a three-hour tour of the architecture of Paris with architect Albert Speer and sculptor Arno Breker in his only visit to the city.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Cold War: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson meets with Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin in Glassboro, New Jersey for the three-day Glassboro Summit Conference.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon are crowned King and Queen of England.
name: Catherine of Aragon

text: English King Henry VIII commands his fourth wife, Anne of Cleves, to leave the court.
name: Anne of Cleves

text: The Diary of a Young Girl (better known as The Diary of Anne Frank) is published.
name: Anne Frank

text: Roman emperor Elagabalus adopts his cousin Alexander Severus as his heir and receives the title of Caesar.
name: Alexander Severus

text: Lavrentiy Beria, head of MVD, is arrested by Nikita Khrushchev and other members of the Politburo.
name: Lavrentiy Beria

text: Cold War: U.S. President John F. Kennedy gave his "Ich bin ein Berliner" speech, underlining the support of the United States for democratic West Germany shortly after Soviet-supported East Germany erected the Berlin Wall.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Karol Wojtyła (later John Paul II) made a cardinal by Pope Paul VI.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: Pope Benedict XVI reinstates the traditional laws of papal election in which a successful candidate must receive two-thirds of the votes.
name: Pope Benedict XVI

text: Amerigo Vespucci sights what is now Amapá State in Brazil.
name: Amerigo Vespucci

text: Sengoku period of Japan: The combined forces of Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu are victorious in the Battle of Nagashino.
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: American Revolutionary War: Thomas Hickey, Continental Army private and bodyguard to General George Washington, is hanged for mutiny and sedition.
name: George Washington

text: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria and his wife Sophie are assassinated in Sarajevo; this is the casus belli of World War I.
name: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria

text: On the 600th anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo, Slobodan Milošević delivers the Gazimestan speech at the site of the historic battle.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: Slobodan Milošević is extradited to the ICTY in The Hague to stand trial.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: Jacques Cartier is the first European to reach Prince Edward Island.
name: Jacques Cartier

text: The Globe Theatre in London, built by William Shakespeare's playing company, the Lord Chamberlain's Men, burns to the ground.
name: William Shakespeare

text: Charles I of England defeats a Parliamentarian detachment at the Battle of Cropredy Bridge.
name: Charles I of England

text: King Henry II of France is mortally wounded in a jousting match against Gabriel, comte de Montgomery.
name: Henry II of France

text: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln grants Yosemite Valley to California for "public use, resort and recreation".
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Albert Einstein sends the article On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies, in which he introduces special relativity, for publication in Annalen der Physik.
name: Albert Einstein

text: The Night of the Long Knives, Adolf Hitler's violent purge of his political rivals in Germany, takes place.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Pope Paul VI issues the Credo of the People of God.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: Joint reading of Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace's papers on evolution to the Linnean Society of London.
name: Alfred Russel Wallace

text: Battle of Yamazaki: Toyotomi Hideyoshi defeats Akechi Mitsuhide.
name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi

text: Victor Emmanuel II of Italy enters Rome after having conquered it from the Papal States.
name: Victor Emmanuel II of Italy

text: British-Italian engineer Guglielmo Marconi obtains a patent for radio in London.
name: Guglielmo Marconi

text: Jean Sibelius' Finlandia receives its première performance in Helsinki with the Helsinki Philharmonic Society conducted by Robert Kajanus.
name: Jean Sibelius

text: Civil rights movement: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act of 1964 meant to prohibit segregation in public places.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: French and Indian War: George Washington surrenders Fort Necessity to French forces.
name: George Washington

text: American Revolutionary War: George Washington takes command of the Continental Army at Cambridge, Massachusetts.
name: George Washington

text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter signs the first directive for secret aid to the opponents of the pro-Soviet regime in Kabul.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: Henry David Thoreau moves into a small cabin on Walden Pond in Concord, Massachusetts. Thoreau's account of his two years there, Walden, will become a touchstone of the environmental movement.
name: Henry David Thoreau

text: The founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, joins Sindh-Madrasa-tul-Islam, Karachi.
name: Muhammad Ali

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Freedom of Information Act into United States law. The act went into effect the next year.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Space Shuttle program: Columbia lands at Edwards Air Force Base at the end of the program's final test flight, STS-4. President Ronald Reagan declares the Space Shuttle to be operational.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Isaac Newton publishes Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica.
name: Isaac Newton

text: The explorer Jacques Cartier lands at St. Malo at the end of his second expedition to North America. He returns with none of the gold he expected to find.
name: Jacques Cartier

text: King Philip II of Spain, consort of Queen Mary I of England, sets out from Dover to war with France, which eventually resulted in the loss of the city of Calais, the last English possession on the continent, and Mary I never seeing her husband again.
name: Philip II of Spain

text: Pope Benedict XIV suppresses the Patriarchate of Aquileia and establishes from its territory the Archdiocese of Udine and Gorizia.
name: Pope Benedict XIV

text: Louis Pasteur successfully tests his vaccine against rabies on Joseph Meister, a boy who was bitten by a rabid dog.
name: Louis Pasteur

text: Anne Frank and her family go into hiding in the "Secret Annexe" above her father's office in an Amsterdam warehouse.
name: Anne Frank

text: Jacques Cartier makes his first contact with aboriginal peoples in what is now Canada.
name: Jacques Cartier

text: Four conspirators in the assassination of Abraham Lincoln are hanged.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: US President Ronald Reagan nominates Sandra Day O'Connor to become the first female member of the Supreme Court of the United States.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Cold War: Samantha Smith, a US schoolgirl, flies to the Soviet Union at the invitation of Secretary General Yuri Andropov.
name: Yuri Andropov

text: Charles II of England grants John Clarke a Royal charter to Rhode Island.
name: Charles II of England

text: Promulgation of the Bayonne Statute, a royal charter Joseph Bonaparte intended as the basis for his rule as king of Spain.
name: Joseph Bonaparte

text: A failed assassination attempt against Iraqi president Saddam Hussein results in the Dujail Massacre over the next several months.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: King Henry VIII of England annuls his marriage to his fourth wife, Anne of Cleves.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: A Bourbon force under Nicolas Catinat withdraws from a smaller Habsburg force under Prince Eugene of Savoy in the Battle of Carpi.
name: Prince Eugene of Savoy

text: George Washington orders the Declaration of Independence to be read out to members of the Continental Army in Manhattan, while thousands of British troops on Staten Island prepare for the Battle of Long Island.
name: George Washington

text: American Revolution: Louis XVI of France declares war on the Kingdom of Great Britain.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: World War II: Six days before Adolf Hitler issues his Directive 16 to the combined Wehrmacht armed forces for Operation Sea Lion, the Kanalkampf shipping attacks begin against British maritime convoys in the leadup to initiating the Battle of Britain.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: King Henry VIII of England marries his sixth and last wife, Catherine Parr, at Hampton Court Palace.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Battle of Aughrim (Julian calendar): The decisive victory of William III of England's forces in Ireland.
name: William III of England

text: Captain James Cook begins his third voyage.
name: James Cook

text: Israeli Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion orders the expulsion of Palestinians from the towns of Lod and Ramla.
name: David Ben-Gurion

text: William I of Scotland, a key rebel in the Revolt of 1173-74, is captured at Alnwick by forces loyal to Henry II of England.
name: Henry II of England

text: Journalist and French revolutionary Jean-Paul Marat is assassinated in his bathtub by Charlotte Corday, a member of the opposing political faction.
name: Jean-Paul Marat

text: Vice President George H. W. Bush becomes the Acting President for the day when President Ronald Reagan undergoes surgery to remove polyps from his colon.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: In a decree called the Gleichschaltung, Adolf Hitler abolishes all German political parties except the Nazis.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: In the Wardha session of Congress, the "Quit India" resolution is approved, authorising Mahatma Gandhi to campaign for India's independence from Britain.
name: Mahatma Gandhi

text: Swedish-Novgorodian Wars: A Novgorodian army led by Alexander Nevsky defeats the Swedes in the Battle of the Neva.
name: Alexander Nevsky

text: Napoleonic Wars: Napoleon Bonaparte surrenders aboard HMS Bellerophon.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Ralph Waldo Emerson delivers the Divinity School Address at Harvard Divinity School, discounting Biblical miracles and declaring Jesus a great man, but not God. The Protestant community reacts with outrage.
name: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: In his book Clinical Psychiatry, Emil Kraepelin gives a name to Alzheimer's disease, naming it after his colleague Alois Alzheimer.
name: Alois Alzheimer

text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter gives his "malaise speech".
name: Jimmy Carter

text: Jacques Cartier, navigator and explorer, returns home to St. Malo after claiming Stadacona (Quebec), Hochelaga (Montereal) and the River of Canada (St. Lawrence River) region for France.
name: Jacques Cartier

text: American Civil War: At the order of President Abraham Lincoln, Union troops begin a 25-mile march into Virginia for what will become the First Battle of Bull Run, the first major land battle of the war.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Iraqi President Ahmed Hassan al-Bakr resigns and is replaced by Saddam Hussein.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: John F. Kennedy Jr., his wife, Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, and her sister, Lauren Bessette, die when the aircraft he is piloting crashes into the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Martha's Vineyard.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Hundred Years' War: Charles VII of France is crowned the King of France in the Reims Cathedral after a successful campaign by Joan of Arc.
name: Charles VII of France

text: King George I of Great Britain sails down the River Thames with a barge of 50 musicians, where George Frideric Handel's Water Music is premiered.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: Former emperor Peter III of Russia is murdered.
name: Peter III of Russia

text: Tsar Nicholas II of Russia and his immediate family and retainers are executed by Bolshevik Chekists at the Ipatiev House in Yekaterinburg, Russia.
name: Nicholas II of Russia

text: World War II: At Sainte-Foy-de-Montgommery in Normandy, Field Marshal Erwin Rommel is seriously injured by Allied aircraft while returning to his headquarters.
name: Erwin Rommel

text: World War II: The main three leaders of the Allied nations, Winston Churchill, Harry S. Truman and Joseph Stalin, meet in the German city of Potsdam to decide the future of a defeated Germany.
name: Winston Churchill

text: The College of Arms is reincorporated by Royal charter signed by Queen Mary I of England and King Philip II of Spain.
name: Philip II of Spain

text: Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of his cantata Erforsche mich, Gott, und erfahre mein Herz, BWV 136, in Leipzig on the eighth Sunday after Trinity.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: Adolf Hitler publishes Mein Kampf.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Great Northern War: A numerically superior Polish-Saxon army of Augustus II the Strong, operating from an advantageous defensive position, is defeated by a Swedish army half its size under the command of King Charles XII in the Battle of Klissow.
name: Augustus II the Strong

text: Field Marshal Ceremony: First occasion in World War II that Adolf Hitler appoints field marshals due to military achievements.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: In a private meeting with U.S. President Ronald Reagan, French President François Mitterrand reveals the existence of the Farewell Dossier, a collection of documents showing the Soviet Union had been stealing American technological research and development.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Richard I of England officially invested as Duke of Normandy.
name: Richard I of England

text: During the first Japanese invasion of Korea, Japanese forces led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi captured Pyongyang, although they were ultimately unable to hold it.
name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi

text: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin consolidates the Commissariats of Home Affairs and National Security to form the NKVD and names Lavrentiy Beria its chief.
name: Lavrentiy Beria

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler survives an assassination attempt led by German Army Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Battle of Taillebourg: Louis IX of France puts an end to the revolt of his vassals Henry III of England and Hugh X of Lusignan.
name: Henry III of England

text: Inauguration of Leopold I of Belgium, first king of the Belgians.
name: Leopold I of Belgium

text: At Adair, Iowa, Jesse James and the James-Younger Gang pull off the first successful train robbery in the American Old West.
name: Jesse James

text: World War II: Claus von Stauffenberg and four fellow conspirators are executed for the July 20 plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: William Shakespeare's play, The Merchant of Venice, is entered on the Stationers' Register. By decree of Queen Elizabeth, the Stationers' Register licensed printed works, giving the Crown tight control over all published material.
name: William Shakespeare

text: Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping is restored to power.
name: Deng Xiaoping

text: Members of 101st Airborne of the United States, aided by Special Forces, attack a compound in Iraq, killing Saddam Hussein's sons Uday and Qusay, along with Mustapha Hussein, Qusay's 14-year-old son, and a bodyguard.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: General Muhammad Naguib leads the Free Officers Movement (formed by Gamal Abdel Nasser, the real power behind the coup) in overthrowing King Farouk of Egypt.
name: Gamal Abdel Nasser

text: Battle of Nocera between Ranulf II of Alife and Roger II of Sicily.
name: Roger II of Sicily

text: French explorer Jacques Cartier plants a cross on the Gaspé Peninsula and takes possession of the territory in the name of Francis I of France.
name: Francis I of France

text: Henry II of France is crowned.
name: Henry II of France

text: The royal wedding of Mary I and Philip II of Spain celebrated at Winchester Cathedral.
name: Philip II of Spain

text: Henry IV of France publicly converts from Protestantism to Roman Catholicism.
name: Henry IV of France

text: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart completes his Symphony No. 40 in G minor (K550).
name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart

text: Napoleon Bonaparte defeats a numerically superior Ottoman army under Mustafa Pasha at the Battle of Abukir.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: World War II: Benito Mussolini is forced out of office by the King (encouraged by the Grand Council of Fascism) and is replaced by Pietro Badoglio.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: Cold War: In a speech John F. Kennedy emphasizes that any attack on Berlin is an attack on NATO.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: The office that would later become the United States Post Office Department is established by the Second Continental Congress. Benjamin Franklin of Pennsylvania takes office as Postmaster General.
name: Benjamin Franklin

text: José de San Martín arrives in Guayaquil, Ecuador, to meet with Simón Bolívar.
name: Simón Bolívar

text: Spanish Civil War: Germany and Italy decide to intervene in the war in support for Francisco Franco and the Nationalist faction.
name: Francisco Franco

text: The Labour Party wins the United Kingdom general election of July 5 by a landslide, removing Winston Churchill from power.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Cold War: Fidel Castro leads an unsuccessful attack on the Moncada Barracks, thus beginning the Cuban Revolution. The movement took the name of the date: 26th of July Movement
name: Fidel Castro

text: Following the World Bank's refusal to fund building the Aswan Dam, Egyptian leader Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalizes the Suez Canal, sparking international condemnation.
name: Gamal Abdel Nasser

text: Battle of Bouvines: Philip II of France decisively defeats Imperial, English and Flemish armies, effectively ending John of England's Angevin Empire.
name: Philip II of France

text: The Jesuit priest Francis Xavier's ship reaches Japan.
name: Francis Xavier

text: French Revolution: Maximilien Robespierre is arrested after encouraging the execution of more than 17,000 "enemies of the Revolution".
name: Maximilien Robespierre

text: Vincent van Gogh shoots himself and dies two days later.
name: Vincent van Gogh

text: Henry VIII of England marries his fifth wife, Catherine Howard.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: French Revolution: Maximilien Robespierre and Louis Antoine de Saint-Just are executed by guillotine in Paris, France.
name: Maximilien Robespierre

text: Peninsular War: Battle of Talavera: Sir Arthur Wellesley's British, Portuguese and Spanish army defeats a French force led by Joseph Bonaparte.
name: Joseph Bonaparte

text: At the age of 18, Vinnie Ream becomes the first and youngest female artist to receive a commission from the United States government for a statue (of Abraham Lincoln).
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: World War II: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin issues Order No. 227. In response to alarming German advances, all those who retreat or otherwise leave their positions without orders to do so are to be tried in a military court, with punishment ranging from duty in a shtrafbat battalion, imprisonment in a Gulag, or execution.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Vietnam War: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson announces his order to increase the number of United States troops in South Vietnam from 75,000 to 125,000.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Founding of the U.S. Army Judge Advocate General's Corps: General George Washington appoints William Tudor as Judge Advocate of the Continental Army.
name: George Washington

text: Adolf Hitler becomes leader of the National Socialist German Workers' Party.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and President of France François Mitterrand sign the agreement to build a tunnel under the English Channel (Channel Tunnel).
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Social Security Act of 1965 into law, establishing Medicare and Medicaid.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Jacques Cœur is arrested by order of Charles VII of France.
name: Charles VII of France

text: The Holocaust: Under instructions from Adolf Hitler, Nazi official Hermann Göring orders SS General Reinhard Heydrich to "submit to me as soon as possible a general plan of the administrative material and financial measures necessary for carrying out the desired Final Solution of the Jewish question."
name: Reinhard Heydrich

text: At Idlewild Field in New York, New York International Airport (later renamed John F. Kennedy International Airport) is dedicated.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Fidel Castro hands over power to his brother, Raúl.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Louis XI of France founds the chivalric order called the Order of Saint Michael in Amboise.
name: Louis XI of France

text: British scientist Joseph Priestley discovers oxygen gas, corroborating the prior discovery of this element by German-Swedish chemist Carl Wilhelm Scheele.
name: Carl Wilhelm Scheele

text: The Olympics opened in Berlin with a ceremony presided over by Adolf Hitler.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Josip Broz Tito reads the resolution "Manifesto of constitutional congress of KPH" to the constitutive congress of KPH (Croatian Communist Party) in woods near Samobor.
name: Josip Broz Tito

text: Charles X of France abdicates the throne in favor of his grandson Henri.
name: Charles X of France

text: Reichskanzler Adolf Hitler becomes Führer of Germany following the death of President Paul von Hindenburg.
name: Paul von Hindenburg

text: Albert Einstein and Leo Szilard write a letter to Franklin D. Roosevelt, urging him to begin the Manhattan Project to develop a nuclear weapon.
name: Albert Einstein

text: World War II: The Motor Torpedo Boat PT-109 is rammed by the Japanese destroyer Amagiri and sinks. Lt. John F. Kennedy, future U.S. president, saves all but two of his crew.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: The theatre La Scala in Milan is inaugurated with the première of Antonio Salieri's Europa riconosciuta.
name: Antonio Salieri

text: First War of Scottish Independence: James Douglas leads a raid into Weardale and almost kills Edward III of England.
name: Edward III of England

text: The Holocaust: A tip from a Dutch informer leads the Gestapo to a sealed-off area in an Amsterdam warehouse, where they find and arrest Jewish diarist Anne Frank, her family, and four others.
name: Anne Frank

text: Vietnam War: At the apartment of French intermediary Jean Sainteny in Paris, American representative Henry Kissinger and North Vietnamese representative Xuân Thuỷ begin secret peace negotiations. The negotiations will eventually fail.
name: Henry Kissinger

text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter signs legislation creating the United States Department of Energy.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: American actress Marilyn Monroe is found dead at her home from a drug overdose.
name: Marilyn Monroe

text: A group of red guards at Experimental High in Beijing, including Deng Rong and Liu Pingping, daughters of Deng Xiaoping and Liu Shaoqi respectively, beat the deputy vice principal, Bian Zhongyun, to death with sticks after accusing her of counter-revolutionary revisionism, producing one of the first fatalities of the Cultural Revolution.
name: Deng Xiaoping

text: President Ronald Reagan fires 11,359 striking air-traffic controllers who ignored his order for them to return to work.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Peruvian War of Independence: Patriot forces led by Simón Bolívar defeat the Spanish Royalist army in the Battle of Junín.
name: Simón Bolívar

text: US President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Voting Rights Act of 1965 into law.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: George Washington orders the creation of the Badge of Military Merit to honor soldiers wounded in battle. It is later renamed to the more poetic Purple Heart.
name: George Washington

text: U.S. President George Washington invokes the Militia Acts of 1792 to suppress the Whiskey Rebellion in western Pennsylvania.
name: George Washington

text: Simón Bolívar triumphs over Spain in the Battle of Boyacá.
name: Simón Bolívar

text: Vietnam War: The U.S. Congress passes the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution giving U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson broad war powers to deal with North Vietnamese attacks on American forces.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter declares a federal emergency at Love Canal due to toxic waste that had been disposed of negligently.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: The cornerstone for Tycho Brahe's Uraniborg observatory is laid on the island of Hven.
name: Tycho Brahe

text: Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus takes oath as Chief Adviser to form an interim government in Bangladesh.
name: Muhammad Yunus

text: American Transcendentalist philosopher Henry David Thoreau publishes his memoir Walden.
name: Henry David Thoreau

text: Dmitri Shostakovich's 7th symphony premiers in a besieged Leningrad.
name: Dmitri Shostakovich

text: Tate-LaBianca murders: Followers of Charles Manson murder pregnant actress Sharon Tate (wife of Roman Polanski), coffee heiress Abigail Folger, Polish actor Wojciech Frykowski, men's hairstylist Jay Sebring and recent high-school graduate Steven Parent.
name: Charles Manson

text: The Treaty of Nonsuch signed by Elizabeth I of England and the Dutch Rebels.
name: Elizabeth I of England

text: P. T. Barnum begins his career as a showman and circus entrepreneur by exhibiting Joice Heth, an octogenerian African slave whom he claims was George Washington's nursemaid.
name: George Washington

text: A day after murdering Sharon Tate and four others, members of Charles Manson's cult kill Leno and Rosemary LaBianca.
name: Charles Manson

text: Japanese American internment: U.S. President Ronald Reagan signs the Civil Liberties Act of 1988, providing $20,000 payments to Japanese Americans who were either interned in or relocated by the United States during World War II.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Rodrigo de Borja is elected as Head of the Catholic Church, taking the name Pope Alexander VI.
name: Pope Alexander VI

text: "We begin bombing in five minutes": United States President Ronald Reagan, while running for re-election, jokes while preparing to make his weekly Saturday address on National Public Radio.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Charles de La Vieuville is arrested and replaced by Cardinal Richelieu as the French king's chief advisor.
name: Cardinal Richelieu

text: The Treaty of Noyon between France and Spain is signed. Francis I of France recognizes Charles's claim to Naples, and Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, recognizes Francis's claim to Milan.
name: Francis I of France

text: Michael Servetus is arrested by John Calvin in Geneva, Switzerland as a heretic.
name: Michael Servetus

text: The French king Louis XIII appoints Cardinal Richelieu as prime minister.
name: Cardinal Richelieu

text: Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of Nimm von uns, Herr, du treuer Gott, BWV 101, a chorale cantata on a famous tune.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: King Louis XVI of France is formally arrested by the National Tribunal, and declared an enemy of the people.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: Portuguese Crisis of 1383-85: Battle of Aljubarrota: Portuguese forces commanded by John I of Portugal defeat the Castilian army of John I of Castile.
name: John I of Portugal

text: World War II: Winston Churchill and Franklin D. Roosevelt sign the Atlantic Charter of war stating postwar aims.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Lech Wałęsa leads strikes at the Gdańsk, Poland shipyards.
name: Lech Wałęsa

text: Mongol invasion of Japan: The Mongolian fleet of Kublai Khan is destroyed by a "divine wind" for the second time in the Battle of Kōan.
name: Kublai Khan

text: Pope Sixtus IV consecrates the Sistine Chapel.
name: Pope Sixtus IV

text: Jesuit priest Francis Xavier comes ashore at Kagoshima (Traditional Japanese date: 22 July 1549).
name: Francis Xavier

text: Battle of the Spurs (Battle of Guinegate): King Henry VIII of England and his Imperial allies defeat French Forces who are then forced to retreat.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Cesare Borgia, son of Pope Alexander VI, becomes the first person in history to resign the cardinalate; later that same day, King Louis XII of France names him Duke of Valentinois.
name: Pope Alexander VI

text: Austro-Turkish War of 1716-18: The month-long Siege of Belgrade ends with Prince Eugene of Savoy's Austrian troops capturing the city from the Ottoman Empire.
name: Prince Eugene of Savoy

text: Pope Benedict XIV, previously known as Prospero Lambertini, succeeds Clement XII as the 247th Pope.
name: Pope Benedict XIV

text: Classical composer Luigi Boccherini receives a pay rise of 12,000 reals from his employer, the Infante Luis, Count of Chinchón.
name: Luigi Boccherini

text: World War II: The U.S. Seventh Army under General George S. Patton arrives in Messina, Italy, followed several hours later by the British 8th Army under Field Marshal Bernard Montgomery, thus completing the Allied conquest of Sicily.
name: George S. Patton

text: World War II: First Québec Conference of Winston Churchill, Franklin D. Roosevelt, and William Lyon Mackenzie King begins.
name: Winston Churchill

text: The Senate of Finland is established in the Grand Duchy of Finland after the official adoption of the Statute of the Government Council by Tsar Alexander I of Russia.
name: Alexander I of Russia

text: Pope Pius II is elected the 211th Pope.
name: Pope Pius II

text: The German referendum of 1934 approves Adolf Hitler's appointment as head of state with the title of Führer.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Cold War: The CIA and MI6 help to overthrow the government of Mohammad Mosaddegh in Iran and reinstate the Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi

text: Dissolution of the Soviet Union: The August Coup begins when Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev is placed under house arrest while on holiday in the town of Foros, Ukraine.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: In Belgrade, Yugoslavia, tens of thousands of Serbians rally to demand the resignation of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia President Slobodan Milošević.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: Richard I of England initiates the Massacre at Ayyadieh, leaving 2,600-3,000 Muslim hostages dead.
name: Richard I of England

text: Charles Darwin first publishes his theory of evolution through natural selection in The Journal of the Proceedings of the Linnean Society of London, alongside Alfred Russel Wallace's same theory.
name: Alfred Russel Wallace

text: Sun Yat-sen, Song Jiaoren, and others establish the Tongmenghui, a Republican, anti-Qing revolutionary organisation, in Tokyo, Japan.
name: Sun Yat-sen

text: In Mexico City, exiled Russian revolutionary Leon Trotsky is fatally wounded with an ice axe by Ramón Mercader. He dies the next day.
name: Leon Trotsky

text: World War II: British Prime Minister Winston Churchill makes the fourth of his famous wartime speeches, containing the line "Never was so much owed by so many to so few".
name: Winston Churchill

text: Dissolution of the Soviet Union, August Coup: More than 100,000 people rally outside the Soviet Union's parliament building protesting the coup aiming to depose President Mikhail Gorbachev.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: A group of Iraqis opposed to the regime of Saddam Hussein take over the Iraqi embassy in Berlin, Germany for five hours before releasing their hostages and surrendering.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Henry the Navigator leads Portuguese forces to victory over the Marinids at the Conquest of Ceuta.
name: Henry the Navigator

text: James Cook formally claims eastern Australia for Great Britain, naming it New South Wales.
name: James Cook

text: Coup attempt against Mikhail Gorbachev collapses.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: James Cook names and lands on Possession Island, and claims the east coast of Australia for Britain as New South Wales.
name: James Cook

text: James Cook's ship HMS Resolution returns to England (Cook having been killed on Hawaii during the voyage).
name: James Cook

text: Mahatma Gandhi forms the Natal Indian Congress (NIC) in order to fight discrimination against Indian traders in Natal.
name: Mahatma Gandhi

text: Pope Paul VI arrives in Bogotá, Colombia. It is the first visit of a pope to Latin America.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: The Congress of Chile votes in favour of a resolution condemning President Salvador Allende's government and demands that he resign or else be unseated through force and new elections.
name: Salvador Allende

text: French explorer Jacques Cartier lands near Quebec City in his third voyage to Canada.
name: Jacques Cartier

text: Battle of Gifu Castle: The eastern forces of Tokugawa Ieyasu defeat the western Japanese clans loyal to Toyotomi Hideyori, leading to the destruction of Gifu Castle and serving as a prelude to the Battle of Sekigahara.
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: Napoleon Bonaparte leaves Egypt for France en route to seizing power.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Saddam Hussein appears on Iraqi state television with a number of Western "guests" (actually hostages) to try to prevent the Gulf War.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: The Holocaust: Adolf Hitler orders the cessation of Nazi Germany's systematic T4 euthanasia program of the mentally ill and the handicapped due to protests, although killings continue for the remainder of the war.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as head of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Galileo Galilei demonstrates his first telescope to Venetian lawmakers.
name: Galileo Galilei

text: Battle of St. Jakob an der Birs: A vastly outnumbered force of Swiss Confederates is defeated by the Dauphin Louis (future Louis XI of France) and his army of 'Armagnacs' near Basel.
name: Louis XI of France

text: Captain James Cook sets sail from England on board HMS Endeavour.
name: James Cook

text: Papal conclave: Albino Luciani is elected as Pope John Paul I.
name: Pope John Paul I

text: Pierre Barrière failed an attempt to assassinate Henry IV of France.
name: Henry IV of France

text: William Herschel discovers a new moon of Saturn: Enceladus.
name: William Herschel

text: Pope Innocent VIII succeeds Pope Sixtus IV.
name: Pope Sixtus IV

text: Battle of Mohács: The Ottoman Turks led by Suleiman the Magnificent defeat and kill the last Jagiellonian king of Hungary and Bohemia.
name: Suleiman the Magnificent

text: Toyotomi Hideyoshi issues a nationwide sword hunting ordinance, disarming the peasantry so as to firmly separate the samurai and commoner classes, prevent peasant uprisings, and further centralise his own power.
name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi

text: Michael Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction.
name: Michael Faraday

text: American experimental composer John Cage's 4’33” premieres at Maverick Concert Hall, played by American pianist David Tudor.
name: John Cage

text: Leading Egyptian thinker Sayyid Qutb is executed for plotting the assassination of President Gamal Abdel Nasser.
name: Gamal Abdel Nasser

text: Pope Paul II succeeds Pope Pius II as the 211th pope.
name: Pope Pius II

text: Tokugawa Ieyasu enters Edo Castle. (Traditional Japanese date: August 1, 1590)
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: Fanni Kaplan shoots and seriously injures Bolshevik leader Vladimir Lenin, which along with the assassination of Bolshevik senior official Moisei Uritsky days earlier, prompts the decree for Red Terror.
name: Vladimir Lenin

text: King Henry V of England dies of dysentery while in France. His son, Henry VI, becomes King of England at the age of nine months.
name: Henry V of England

text: Pope Paul III excommunicates English King Henry VIII from the church. He drew up a papal bull of excommunication which began Eius qui immobilis.
name: Pope Paul III

text: Saddam Hussein's troops seized Irbil after the Kurdish Masoud Barzani appealed for help to defeat his Kurdish rival PUK.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Lady Anne Boleyn is made Marquess of Pembroke by her fiancé, King Henry VIII of England.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Claudio Monteverdi's musical work Vespro della Beata Vergine (Vespers for the Blessed Virgin) is first published, printed in Venice and dedicated to Pope Paul V.
name: Claudio Monteverdi

text: Emma Nutt becomes the world's first female telephone operator when she is recruited by Alexander Graham Bell to the Boston Telephone Dispatch Company.
name: Alexander Graham Bell

text: The Treaty of Jaffa is signed between Richard I of England and Saladin, leading to the end of the Third Crusade.
name: Richard I of England

text: American Civil War: United States President Abraham Lincoln reluctantly restores Union General George B. McClellan to full command after General John Pope's disastrous defeat at the Second Battle of Bull Run.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Transnistria is unilaterally proclaimed a Soviet republic; the Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev declares the decision null and void.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Richard I of England (a.k.a. Richard "the Lionheart") is crowned at Westminster.
name: Richard I of England

text: The death of Oliver Cromwell; Richard Cromwell becomes Lord Protector of England.
name: Oliver Cromwell

text: Holocaust: Diarist Anne Frank and her family are placed on the last transport train from the Westerbork transit camp to the Auschwitz concentration camp, arriving three days later.
name: Anne Frank

text: New Caledonia is first sighted by Europeans, during the second voyage of Captain James Cook.
name: James Cook

text: Salvador Allende is elected President of Chile.
name: Salvador Allende

text: Pope Benedict XVI becomes the longest-lived pope, 93 years, four months, 16 days, surpassing Pope Leo XIII, who died in 1903.
name: Pope Benedict XVI

text: Alexander Farnese's army forces Henry IV of France to lift the siege of Paris.
name: Henry IV of France

text: In France, Robert Schuman becomes President of the Council while being Foreign minister; as such, he is the negotiator of the major treaties of the end of World War II.
name: Robert Schuman

text: Cuban Revolution: Fulgencio Batista bombs the revolt in Cienfuegos.
name: Fulgencio Batista

text: Camp David Accords: Menachem Begin and Anwar Sadat begin peace discussions at Camp David, Maryland.
name: Menachem Begin

text: British scientist John Dalton begins using symbols to represent the atoms of different elements.
name: John Dalton

text: Louis the Stammerer is crowned as king of West Francia by Pope John VIII.
name: Louis the Stammerer

text: Third Crusade: Battle of Arsuf: Richard I of England defeats Saladin at Arsuf.
name: Richard I of England

text: Thomas Howard, 4th Duke of Norfolk, is arrested for his role in the Ridolfi plot to assassinate Queen Elizabeth I of England and replace her with Mary, Queen of Scots.
name: Elizabeth I of England

text: The town of Kokkola (Swedish: Karleby) is founded by King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden.
name: Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden

text: Unification of Italy: Giuseppe Garibaldi enters Naples.
name: Giuseppe Garibaldi

text: In Northfield, Minnesota, Jesse James and the James-Younger Gang attempt to rob the town's bank but are driven off by armed citizens.
name: Jesse James

text: French poet Guillaume Apollinaire is arrested and put in jail on suspicion of stealing the Mona Lisa from the Louvre museum.
name: Guillaume Apollinaire

text: Warsaw falls without resistance to a small force under the command of Charles X Gustav of Sweden during The Deluge, making it the first time the city is captured by a foreign army.
name: Charles X Gustav of Sweden

text: Marriage of King George III of the United Kingdom to Duchess Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz.
name: George III of the United Kingdom

text: Rif War: Spanish forces including troops from the Foreign Legion under Colonel Francisco Franco landing at Al Hoceima, Morocco.
name: Francisco Franco

text: Trans International Airlines Flight 863 crashes during takeoff from John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City, killing all 11 aboard.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: In Washington, D.C., the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts is inaugurated, with the opening feature being the premiere of Leonard Bernstein's Mass.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Washington, D.C., the capital of the United States, is named after President George Washington.
name: George Washington

text: Alexander I of Russia confirms the privileges of Baltic provinces.
name: Alexander I of Russia

text: The National Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act is signed into law by U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy is assassinated by adherents of the Dauphin, the future Charles VII of France.
name: Charles VII of France

text: Fourth Battle of Kawanakajima: Takeda Shingen defeats Uesugi Kenshin in the climax of their ongoing conflicts.
name: Takeda Shingen

text: Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of Jesu, der du meine Seele, BWV 78, a chorale cantata based on a passion hymn by Johann Rist.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: Empress Elisabeth of Austria is assassinated by Luigi Lucheni.
name: Empress Elisabeth of Austria

text: Siege of Drogheda ends: Oliver Cromwell's Parliamentarian troops take the town and execute its garrison.
name: Oliver Cromwell

text: Coalition forces, including the famous winged Hussars, led by Polish King John III Sobieski lift the siege laid by Ottoman forces ahead of the Battle of Vienna.
name: John III Sobieski

text: Charles Lindbergh's Des Moines speech accusing the British, Jews and FDR's administration of conspiring for war with Germany.
name: Charles Lindbergh

text: A coup in Chile, headed by General Augusto Pinochet, topples the democratically elected president Salvador Allende.
name: Salvador Allende

text: Battle of Portopí: The Aragonese army under the command of James I of Aragon disembarks at Santa Ponça, Mallorca, with the purpose of conquering the island.
name: James I of Aragon

text: Premiere performance of Gustav Mahler's Symphony No. 8 in Munich (with a chorus of 852 singers and an orchestra of 171 players. Mahler's rehearsal assistant conductor was Bruno Walter).
name: Gustav Mahler

text: Adolf Hitler demands autonomy and self-determination for the Germans of the Sudetenland region of Czechoslovakia.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: World War II: Benito Mussolini is rescued from house arrest by German commando forces led by Otto Skorzeny.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: US President John F. Kennedy delivers his "We choose to go to the Moon" speech at Rice University.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Ögedei Khan is proclaimed Khagan of the Mongol Empire in Kodoe Aral, Khentii: Mongolia.
name: Ögedei Khan

text: King Louis XVI of France accepts the new constitution.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: "Night of the three Caliphs": Harun al-Rashid becomes the Abbasid caliph upon the death of his brother al-Hadi. Birth of Harun's son al-Ma'mun.
name: Harun al-Rashid

text: George Frideric Handel completes his oratorio Messiah.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: American Revolutionary War: Review of the French troops under General Rochambeau by General George Washington at Verplanck's Point, New York.
name: George Washington

text: Congo Crisis: Mobutu Sese Seko seizes power in a military coup, suspending parliament and the constitution.
name: Mobutu Sese Seko

text: The first American saint, Elizabeth Ann Seton, is canonized by Pope Paul VI.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: HMS Beagle, with Charles Darwin aboard, reaches the Galápagos Islands. The ship lands at Chatham or San Cristobal, the easternmost of the archipelago.
name: Charles Darwin

text: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill meet in Quebec as part of the Octagon Conference to discuss strategy.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Marilyn Monroe's iconic skirt scene is shot during filming for The Seven Year Itch.
name: Marilyn Monroe

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson, responding to a sniper attack at the University of Texas at Austin, writes a letter to Congress urging the enactment of gun control legislation.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Israeli premier Menachem Begin resigns.
name: Menachem Begin

text: French physicist Augustin-Jean Fresnel, in a "note" read to the Academy of Sciences, reports a direct refraction experiment verifying David Brewster's hypothesis that photoelasticity (as it is now known) is stress-induced birefringence.
name: Augustin-Jean Fresnel

text: The Treaty of Bergerac is signed between King Henry III of France and the Huguenots.
name: Henry III of France

text: World War I: Manfred von Richthofen ("The Red Baron"), a flying ace of the German Luftstreitkräfte, wins his first aerial combat near Cambrai, France.
name: Manfred von Richthofen

text: The first cornerstone of the United States Capitol is laid by George Washington.
name: George Washington

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler orders the deportation of Danish Jews.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Fidel Castro arrives in New York City as the head of the Cuban delegation to the United Nations.
name: Fidel Castro

text: U.N. Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld dies in an air crash while attempting to negotiate peace in the Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
name: Dag Hammarskjöld

text: George Washington's Farewell Address is printed across America as an open letter to the public.
name: George Washington

text: The Council of Europe is founded following a speech by Winston Churchill at the University of Zurich.
name: Winston Churchill

text: The future King Edward VII of the United Kingdom begins the first visit to North America by a Prince of Wales.
name: Edward VII of the United Kingdom

text: The Moomin comics, created by Tove Jansson and Lars Jansson, is published internationally in the London newspaper The Evening News.
name: Tove Jansson

text: Battle of Rymnik: Alexander Suvorov's Russian and allied army defeats superior Ottoman Empire forces.
name: Alexander Suvorov

text: A preliminary version of the Emancipation Proclamation is released by Abraham Lincoln.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: King Philip II of Spain issues cedula, ordering a halt to colonizing efforts in Florida.
name: Philip II of Spain

text: U.S. President John F. Kennedy nominates African American civil rights lawyer Thurgood Marshall to the Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, although pro-segregation Southern senators manage to delay his confirmation until September 11, 1962.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Pope Alexander VI issues the papal bull Dudum siquidem to the Spanish, extending the grant of new lands he made them in Inter caetera.
name: Pope Alexander VI

text: George Washington appoints Thomas Jefferson the first United States Secretary of State.
name: George Washington

text: Albert Einstein publishes the third of his Annus Mirabilis papers, introducing the special theory of relativity.
name: Albert Einstein

text: In Chicago, the first televised debate takes place between presidential candidates Richard M. Nixon and John F. Kennedy.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: The Society of Jesus (Jesuits) receives its charter from Pope Paul III.
name: Pope Paul III

text: Jean-François Champollion officially informs the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres in France that he has deciphered the Rosetta Stone.
name: Jean-François Champollion

text: King James I of Aragon conquers Valencia from the Moors. Shortly thereafter, he proclaims himself king of Valencia.
name: James I of Aragon

text: The Battle of Alcolea causes Queen Isabella II of Spain to flee to France.
name: Isabella II of Spain

text: Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser dies of a heart attack in Cairo.
name: Gamal Abdel Nasser

text: Suleiman the Magnificent is proclaimed sultan of the Ottoman Empire.
name: Suleiman the Magnificent

text: Georges Bizet's opera Les pêcheurs de perles, premiered in Paris.
name: Georges Bizet

text: The coronation of Queen Mary I of England is held at Westminster Abbey.
name: Mary I of England

text: Russians under Alexander Suvorov defeat the Turks at Kinburn.
name: Alexander Suvorov

text: The Metamorphosis written by Franz Kafka is published in the German journal Die Weißen Blätter
name: Franz Kafka

text: Spanish Civil War: Francisco Franco is named head of the Nationalist government of Spain.
name: Francisco Franco

text: Pope John Paul II begins his first pastoral visit to the United States.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: George Washington proclaims Thursday November 26, 1789 a Thanksgiving Day.
name: George Washington

text: The last Thursday in November is declared as Thanksgiving Day by U.S. President Abraham Lincoln.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: The Gregorian Calendar is introduced by Pope Gregory XIII.
name: Pope Gregory XIII

text: American Revolutionary War: Troops under George Washington are repelled by British troops under William Howe.
name: George Washington

text: Pope Paul VI begins the first papal visit to the Americas.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: A reactor at the Enrico Fermi Nuclear Generating Station near Detroit suffers a partial meltdown.
name: Enrico Fermi

text: Mass demonstrations in Serbia force the resignation of Slobodan Milošević.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: Pope John Paul II becomes the first pontiff to visit the White House.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat is murdered by Islamic extremists.
name: Anwar Sadat

text: Uppsala University is inaugurated after receiving its corporate rights from Pope Sixtus IV in February the same year.
name: Pope Sixtus IV

text: Mother Teresa establishes the Missionaries of Charity.
name: Mother Teresa

text: James I of Aragon founds the Kingdom of Valencia.
name: James I of Aragon

text: Pope John Paul II greets the Dalai Lama during a private audience in Vatican City.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: The Battle of Karbala marks the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali.
name: Husayn ibn Ali

text: The Duke and Duchess of Windsor tour Nazi Germany for 12 days and meet Adolf Hitler on 22 October.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev meet in Iceland to continue discussions about scaling back IRBM arsenals in Europe.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: The Provisional Irish Republican Army fail to assassinate Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and her cabinet.  The bomb kills five people and wounds at least 31 others.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: Robert the Bruce of Scotland defeats King Edward II of England at the Battle of Old Byland, forcing Edward to accept Scotland's independence.
name: Edward II of England

text: Mary, Queen of Scots, goes on trial for conspiracy against Queen Elizabeth I of England.
name: Elizabeth I of England

text: The Treaty of Schönbrunn is signed, ending the War of the Fifth Coalition, the final successful war in Napoleon Bonaparte's military career.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Vice President Hosni Mubarak is elected as the President of Egypt, one week after the assassination of Anwar Sadat.
name: Anwar Sadat

text: U.S. President Ronald Reagan proclaims a War on Drugs.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Yasser Arafat, Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres receive the Nobel Peace Prize for their role in the establishment of the Oslo Accords and the framing of future Palestinian self government.
name: Shimon Peres

text: Queen Marie Antoinette of France is tried and convicted of treason.
name: Marie Antoinette

text: Soviet Union leader Mikhail Gorbachev is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to lessen Cold War tensions and open up his nation.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Empress Wu Zetian ascends to the throne of the Tang dynasty and proclaims herself ruler of the Chinese Empire.
name: Wu Zetian

text: French Revolution: Queen Marie Antoinette is executed.
name: Marie Antoinette

text: Simón Bolívar sentences Manuel Piar to death for challenging the racial-caste in Venezuela.
name: Simón Bolívar

text: William Rowan Hamilton invents quaternions, a three-dimensional system of complex numbers.
name: William Rowan Hamilton

text: Adolf Hitler delivers his first public address at a meeting of the German Workers' Party.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Cuban revolutionary Fidel Castro delivers his "History Will Absolve Me" speech, and is sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment by the Fulgencio Batista government for leading an attack on the Moncada Barracks.
name: Fulgencio Batista

text: Cuban Missile Crisis begins: U.S. President John F. Kennedy is informed of photos taken on October 14 by a U-2 showing nuclear missiles (the crisis will last for 13 days starting from this point).
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Leonid Brezhnev becomes leader of the Soviet Communist Party, while Alexei Kosygin becomes the head of government.
name: Leonid Brezhnev

text: Yasunari Kawabata becomes the first Japanese person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
name: Yasunari Kawabata

text: Henry Kissinger and Lê Đức Thọ are awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
name: Henry Kissinger

text: Cardinal Karol Wojtyła is elected to the papacy as Pope John Paul II, he becomes the first non-Italian pontiff since 1523.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Empress Wu Zetian establishes the Zhou Dynasty of China.
name: Wu Zetian

text: Anti-Catholic posters appear in Paris and other cities supporting Huldrych Zwingli's position on the Mass.
name: Huldrych Zwingli

text: The nine regicides who signed the death warrant of Charles I of England are hanged, drawn and quartered.
name: Charles I of England

text: Charles II of England sells Dunkirk to Louis XIV of France for 40,000 pounds.
name: Charles II of England

text: Al Capone is convicted of income tax evasion.
name: Al Capone

text: Albert Einstein flees Nazi Germany and moves to the United States.
name: Albert Einstein

text: Mother Teresa is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
name: Mother Teresa

text: The East German Politburo votes to remove Erich Honecker from his role as General Secretary.
name: Erich Honecker

text: In Japan the fourth Battle of Kawanakajima is fought between the forces of Uesugi Kenshin and Takeda Shingen, resulting in a draw.
name: Takeda Shingen

text: King Philip II of Spain sends his third and final armada against England, but it ends in failure due to storms. The remaining ships are captured or sunk by the English.
name: Philip II of Spain

text: World War II: The state funeral of Field Marshal Erwin Rommel takes place in Ulm, Germany.
name: Erwin Rommel

text: Martin Luther becomes a doctor of theology.
name: Martin Luther

text: New Ross town in Ireland surrenders to Oliver Cromwell.
name: Oliver Cromwell

text: Mother Teresa is beatified by Pope John Paul II.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Saddam Hussein goes on trial in Baghdad for crimes against humanity.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Martin Luther joins the theological faculty of the University of Wittenberg.
name: Martin Luther

text: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeats the leaders of rival Japanese clans in the Battle of Sekigahara and becomes shōgun of Japan.
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: Florence Nightingale and a staff of 38 nurses are sent to the Crimean War.
name: Florence Nightingale

text: Moshe Dayan resigns from the Israeli government because of strong disagreements with Prime Minister Menachem Begin over policy towards the Arabs.
name: Menachem Begin

text: Jean-Paul Sartre is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, though he does not accept the prize.
name: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: Adolf Hitler and Francisco Franco meet at Hendaye to discuss the possibility of Spain entering the Second World War.
name: Francisco Franco

text: Chartres Cathedral is dedicated in the presence of King Louis IX of France.
name: Louis IX of France

text: Felim O'Neill of Kinard, the leader of the Irish Rebellion, issues his Proclamation of Dungannon, justifying the uprising and declaring continued loyalty to King Charles I of England.
name: Charles I of England

text: Hundred Years' War: Henry V of England, with his lightly armoured infantry and archers, defeats the heavily armoured French cavalry in the Battle of Agincourt.
name: Henry V of England

text: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky’s Piano Concerto No. 1 in B♭ minor, Op. 23 premieres in Boston, Massachusetts, with Benjamin Johnson Lang as conductor and Hans von Bülow as soloist.
name: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky

text: World War II: Heinrich Himmler orders a crackdown on the Edelweiss Pirates, a loosely organized youth culture in Nazi Germany that had assisted army deserters and others to hide from the Third Reich.
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: The Treaty of Ripon is signed, restoring peace between Covenanter Scotland and King Charles I of England.
name: Charles I of England

text: Unification of Italy: The Expedition of the Thousand ends when Giuseppe Garibaldi presents his conquests to King Victor Emmanuel of Sardinia.
name: Giuseppe Garibaldi

text: World War I: Erich Ludendorff, quartermaster-general of the Imperial German Army, is dismissed by Kaiser Wilhelm II for refusing to cooperate in peace negotiations.
name: Erich Ludendorff

text: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi crowns himself Emperor of Iran.
name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi

text: Condemned as a heretic, Michael Servetus is burned at the stake just outside Geneva.
name: Michael Servetus

text: Ronald Reagan delivers a speech on behalf of the Republican candidate for president, Barry Goldwater. The speech launches his political career and comes to be known as "A Time for Choosing".
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Cold War: Ronald Reagan suspends construction of the new U.S. Embassy in Moscow due to Soviet listening devices in the building structure.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: The novel Gulliver's Travels written by Jonathan Swift is published.
name: Jonathan Swift

text: Italian fascists led by Benito Mussolini march on Rome and take over the Italian government.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: Pope Paul VI promulgates Nostra aetate, by which the Roman Catholic Church officially recognizes the legitimacy of non-Christian faiths.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: Russian homage to the King of Poland, Sigismund III Vasa.
name: Sigismund III Vasa

text: Israel's prime minister David Ben-Gurion and five of his ministers are injured when Moshe Dwek throws a grenade into the Knesset.
name: David Ben-Gurion

text: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher opens the last stretch of the M25 motorway.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: Ranulf of Apulia defeats Roger II of Sicily at the Battle of Rignano, securing his position as duke until his death two years later.
name: Roger II of Sicily

text: The Eighth Crusade ends by an agreement between Charles I of Anjou (replacing his deceased brother King Louis IX of France) and the Hafsid dynasty of Tunis, Tunisia.
name: Louis IX of France

text: Simón Bolívar becomes President of the Third Republic of Venezuela.
name: Simón Bolívar

text: Due to "violations of Vladimir Lenin's precepts", it is decreed that Joseph Stalin's body be removed from its place of honour inside Lenin's tomb and buried near the Kremlin Wall with a plain granite marker.
name: Vladimir Lenin

text: Prince Juan Carlos I of Spain becomes acting head of state, taking over for the country's ailing dictator, Gen. Francisco Franco.
name: Juan Carlos I of Spain

text: Protestant Reformation: Martin Luther posts his 95 Theses on the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg.
name: Martin Luther

text: The Parliament of Finland approved the Prohibition Act, but the law was not implemented because it was not ratified by Tsar Nicholas II of Russia.
name: Nicholas II of Russia

text: Benito Mussolini is made Prime Minister of Italy.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: In the Soviet Union, Joseph Stalin's body is removed from Lenin's Mausoleum, also known as the Lenin Tomb.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Vietnam War October surprise: Citing progress with the Paris peace talks, US President Lyndon B. Johnson announces to the nation that he has ordered a complete cessation of "all air, naval, and artillery bombardment of North Vietnam" effective November 1.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: William Shakespeare's tragedy Othello is performed for the first time, at Whitehall Palace in London.
name: William Shakespeare

text: William III of Orange sets out a second time from Hellevoetsluis in the Netherlands to seize the crowns of England, Scotland and Ireland from King James II of England during the Glorious Revolution.
name: James II of England

text: Edmund Burke publishes Reflections on the Revolution in France, in which he predicts that the French Revolution will end in a disaster.
name: Edmund Burke

text: Napoleon Bonaparte invades Austria during the War of the Third Coalition.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: American Civil War: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln appoints George B. McClellan as the commander of the Union Army, replacing General Winfield Scott.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Buffalo Bill, 15 of his Native Americans, and Annie Oakley were filmed by Thomas Edison in his Black Maria Studio in West Orange, New Jersey.
name: Buffalo Bill

text: Lahti, a city in Finland, is granted city rights by Tsar Nicholas II of Russia, the last Grand Duke of Finland.
name: Nicholas II of Russia

text: Hungarian Revolution: Nikita Khrushchev meets with leaders of other Communist countries to seek their advice on the situation in Hungary, selecting János Kádár as the country's next leader on the advice of Josip Broz Tito.
name: Josip Broz Tito

text: Vietnam War: US President Lyndon B. Johnson and "The Wise Men" conclude that the American people should be given more optimistic reports on the progress of the war.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: U.S. President Ronald Reagan signs a bill creating Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Peace of Etaples between Henry VII of England and Charles VIII of France.
name: Charles VIII of France

text: Giuseppe Garibaldi and his followers are defeated in the Battle of Mentana and fail to end the Pope's Temporal power in Rome (it would be achieved three years later).
name: Giuseppe Garibaldi

text: U Thant is unanimously appointed as the 3rd Secretary-General of the United Nations, becoming the first non-European individual to occupy the post.
name: U Thant

text: Lyndon B. Johnson is elected to a full term as U.S. president, winning 61% of the vote and 44 states, while Washington D.C. residents are able to vote in a presidential election for the first time, casting the majority of their votes for Lyndon Johnson.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Catherine of Aragon (later Henry VIII's first wife) meets Arthur Tudor, Henry VIII's older brother - they would later marry.
name: Catherine of Aragon

text: The future Mary II of England marries William, Prince of Orange; they later jointly reign as William and Mary.
name: Mary II of England

text: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's Symphony No. 36 is performed for the first time in Linz, Austria.
name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart

text: World War II: Disobeying a direct order by Adolf Hitler, General Field Marshal Erwin Rommel begins a retreat of his forces after a costly defeat during the Second Battle of El Alamein. The retreat would ultimately last five months.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Salvador Allende takes office as President of Chile, the first Marxist to become president of a Latin American country through open elections.
name: Salvador Allende

text: Ronald Reagan is elected as the 40th President of the United States, defeating incumbent Jimmy Carter.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Prince William III of Orange lands with a Dutch fleet at Brixham to challenge the rule of King James II of England (James VII of Scotland).
name: James II of England

text: American Civil War: Abraham Lincoln removes George B. McClellan as commander of the Army of the Potomac.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Saddam Hussein, the former president of Iraq, and his co-defendants Barzan Ibrahim al-Tikriti and Awad Hamed al-Bandar, are sentenced to death in the al-Dujail trial for their roles in the 1982 massacre of 148 Shia Muslims.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: The first recorded observation from Earth of the Great Comet of 1577 takes place by Aztec astronomers in Mexico, followed by reports from Italy on November 7 and Japan on November 8. Astronomer Tycho Brahe will track the comet from November 13 until January 26 before it departs the Solar System.
name: Tycho Brahe

text: Abraham Lincoln is elected the 16th president of the United States with only 40% of the popular vote, defeating John C. Breckinridge, John Bell, and Stephen A. Douglas in a four-way race.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: O Ewigkeit, du Donnerwort, BWV 60, a dialogue cantata by Johann Sebastian Bach for Leipzig, was first performed.
name: Johann Sebastian Bach

text: Soviet spy Richard Sorge, a half-Russian, half-German World War I veteran, is hanged by his Japanese captors along with 34 of his ring.
name: Richard Sorge

text: US President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Public Broadcasting Act of 1967, establishing the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Japanese daimyō Dom Justo Takayama is exiled to the Philippines by shōgun Tokugawa Ieyasu for being Christian.
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: The first Council of People's Commissars is formed, including Vladimir Lenin, Leon Trotsky and Joseph Stalin.
name: Vladimir Lenin

text: Beer Hall Putsch: In Munich, Adolf Hitler leads the Nazis in an unsuccessful attempt to overthrow the German government.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: In Munich, Adolf Hitler narrowly escapes the assassination attempt of Georg Elser while celebrating the 16th anniversary of the Beer Hall Putsch.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: John F. Kennedy is elected as the 35th President of the United States, defeating incumbent Vice President Richard Nixon, who would later be elected president in 1968  and 1972.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson signs into law an antitrust exemption allowing the National Football League to merge with the upstart American Football League.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Iraq disarmament crisis: UN Security Council Resolution 1441: The United Nations Security Council unanimously approves a resolution on Iraq, forcing Saddam Hussein to disarm or face "serious consequences".
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Napoleon Bonaparte leads the Coup of 18 Brumaire ending the Directory government, and becoming First Consul of the successor Consulate Government.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Prince George, Duke of Cornwall (later George V of the United Kingdom), becomes Prince of Wales and Earl of Chester.
name: George V of the United Kingdom

text: Battle of Stalingrad: German forces of the 6th Army under general Friedrich Paulus reach finally the river bank of the Volga, capturing 90% of the ruined city of Stalingrad and splitting the remaining Soviet forces into two narrow pockets.
name: Friedrich Paulus

text: Robert McNamara is named president of the Ford Motor Company, becoming the first non-Ford family member to serve in that post. He resigns a month later to join the newly elected John F. Kennedy administration.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Henry Morton Stanley locates missing explorer and missionary, David Livingstone in Ujiji, near Lake Tanganyika, famously greeting him with the words, "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?"
name: David Livingstone

text: Southern Airways Flight 49 from Birmingham, Alabama is hijacked and, at one point, is threatened with crashing into the nuclear installation at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After two days, the plane lands in Havana, Cuba, where the hijackers are jailed by Fidel Castro.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Tycho Brahe observes the supernova SN 1572.
name: Tycho Brahe

text: Adolf Hitler is arrested in Munich for high treason for his role in the Beer Hall Putsch.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Patent number US1781541 is awarded to Albert Einstein and Leó Szilárd for their invention, the Einstein refrigerator.
name: Albert Einstein

text: Leon Trotsky is expelled from the Soviet Communist Party, leaving Joseph Stalin in undisputed control of the Soviet Union.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: World War II: Soviet Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov arrives in Berlin to discuss the possibility of the Soviet Union joining the Axis Powers.
name: Vyacheslav Molotov

text: Iran hostage crisis: In response to the hostage situation in Tehran, U.S. President Jimmy Carter orders a halt to all petroleum imports into the United States from Iran.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: USSR: Yuri Andropov becomes the General Secretary of the Communist Party's Central Committee, succeeding Leonid I. Brezhnev.
name: Yuri Andropov

text: In New York City, American Airlines Flight 587, an Airbus A300 en route to the Dominican Republic, crashes minutes after takeoff from John F. Kennedy International Airport, killing all 260 on board and five on the ground.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: US President Jimmy Carter issues Executive Order 12170, freezing all Iranian assets in the United States in response to the hostage crisis.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: Lech Wałęsa, the leader of Poland's outlawed Solidarity movement, is released after eleven months of internment near the Soviet border.
name: Lech Wałęsa

text: Second Boer War: Battle of Chieveley, a British armored train is ambushed and partially derailed. British lose the battle, with 80 soldiers captured, along with war correspondent Winston Churchill.
name: Winston Churchill

text: The Holocaust: German SS leader Heinrich Himmler orders that Gypsies are to be put "on the same level as Jews and placed in concentration camps".
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: The Anglo-Irish Agreement is signed at Hillsborough Castle by British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Irish Taoiseach Garret FitzGerald.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: While travelling during the Ninth Crusade, Prince Edward becomes King of England upon Henry III of England's death, but he will not return to England for nearly two years to assume the throne.
name: Henry III of England

text: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden was killed at the Battle of Lützen during the Thirty Years' War.
name: Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden

text: David Livingstone becomes the first European to see the Victoria Falls in what is now Zambia-Zimbabwe.
name: David Livingstone

text: Henry VIII of England concludes the Treaty of Westminster, a pledge of mutual aid against the French, with Ferdinand II of Aragon.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Elizabethan era begins: Queen Mary I of England dies and is succeeded by her half-sister Elizabeth I of England.
name: Elizabeth I of England

text: President John F. Kennedy dedicates Washington Dulles International Airport, serving the Washington, D.C., region.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Vietnam War: Acting on optimistic reports that he had been given on November 13, U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson tells the nation that, while much remained to be done, "We are inflicting greater losses than we're taking...We are making progress."
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Actor Arnold Schwarzenegger's tenure as the governor of California began.
name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
