text: World War II: German leader Adolf Hitler and Italian Foreign Minister Galeazzo Ciano meet to discuss Benito Mussolini's disastrous Italian invasion of Greece.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: United States President John F. Kennedy sends 18,000 military advisors to South Vietnam.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: American Civil War: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address at the dedication ceremony for the military cemetery at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Cold War: In Geneva, U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet Union General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev meet for the first time.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Serbian communist representative and future Serbian and Yugoslav president Slobodan Milošević publicly declares that Serbia is under attack from Albanian separatists in Kosovo as well as internal treachery within Yugoslavia and a foreign conspiracy to destroy Serbia and Yugoslavia.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: The French actress Sarah Bernhardt receives the press at the Savoy Hotel in New York at the outset of her first visit since 1896. She talked about her impending tour with a troupe of more than 50 performers and her plans to play the title role in Hamlet.
name: Sarah Bernhardt

text: Cuban Missile Crisis ends: In response to the Soviet Union agreeing to remove its missiles from Cuba, U.S. President John F. Kennedy ends the quarantine of the Caribbean nation.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat becomes the first Arab leader to officially visit Israel, when he meets Israeli prime minister Menachem Begin and speaks before the Knesset in Jerusalem, seeking a permanent peace settlement.
name: Menachem Begin

text: Andrei Chikatilo, one of the Soviet Union's most prolific serial killers, is arrested; he eventually confesses to 56 killings.
name: Andrei Chikatilo

text: The Danish astronomer Ole Rømer presents the first quantitative measurements of the speed of light.
name: Ole Rømer

text: Claude Monet's paintings shown at Gallery Durand-Ruel in Paris.
name: Claude Monet

text: Albert Einstein's paper that leads to the mass-energy equivalence formula, E = mc², is published in the journal Annalen der Physik.
name: Albert Einstein

text: World War II: Battle of Stalingrad: General Friedrich Paulus sends Adolf Hitler a telegram saying that the German 6th Army is surrounded.
name: Friedrich Paulus

text: World War II: Cairo Conference: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Chinese Premier Chiang Kai-shek meet in Cairo, Egypt, to discuss ways to defeat Japan.
name: Winston Churchill

text: U.S. President John F. Kennedy is assassinated and Texas Governor John Connally is seriously wounded by Lee Harvey Oswald, who also kills Dallas Police officer J. D. Tippit after fleeing the scene. Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson is sworn in as the 36th President of the United States afterwards.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Juan Carlos is declared King of Spain following the death of Francisco Franco.
name: Francisco Franco

text: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher withdraws from the Conservative Party leadership election, confirming the end of her Prime-Ministership.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: John Milton publishes Areopagitica, a pamphlet decrying censorship.
name: John Milton

text: Edwin Hubble's discovery, that the Andromeda "nebula" is actually another island galaxy far outside our own Milky Way, is first published in The New York Times.
name: Edwin Hubble

text: Iran-Contra affair: Ronald Reagan signs the top secret National Security Decision Directive 17 (NSDD-17), giving the Central Intelligence Agency the authority to recruit and support Contra rebels in Nicaragua.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Queen lead singer Freddie Mercury announces in a statement that he is HIV-positive. He dies the following day.
name: Freddie Mercury

text: British naturalist Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species is published.
name: Charles Darwin

text: Lee Harvey Oswald, the assassin of President John F. Kennedy, is killed by Jack Ruby on live television. Robert H. Jackson takes a photograph of the shooting that will win the 1964 Pulitzer Prize in Photography.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Albert Einstein presents the field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
name: Albert Einstein

text: Agatha Christie's murder-mystery play The Mousetrap opens at the Ambassadors Theatre in London's West End after a premiere in Nottingham, UK.  It will become the longest continuously running play in history.
name: Agatha Christie

text: State funeral of John F. Kennedy; after lying in state at the United States Capitol, a Requiem Mass takes place at Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle and the President is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Pope John Paul II appoints Joseph Cardinal Ratzinger (the future Pope Benedict XVI) Prefect of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: In the Hawaiian Islands, Captain James Cook becomes the first European to visit Maui.
name: James Cook

text: A national Thanksgiving Day is observed in the United States as proclaimed by President George Washington at the request of Congress.
name: George Washington

text: United States President Abraham Lincoln proclaims November 26 as a national Thanksgiving Day, to be celebrated annually on the final Thursday of November.  Following the Franksgiving controversy from 1939 to 1941, it has been observed on the fourth Thursday in 1942 and subsequent years.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Casablanca, the movie starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, premieres in New York City.
name: Humphrey Bogart

text: Iran-Contra affair: U.S. President Ronald Reagan announces the members of what will become known as the Tower Commission.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Emperor Marcus Aurelius grants his son Commodus the rank of "Imperator" and makes him Supreme Commander of the Roman legions.
name: Marcus Aurelius

text: At the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris, Alfred Nobel signs his last will and testament, setting aside his estate to establish the Nobel Prize after he dies.
name: Alfred Nobel

text: Also sprach Zarathustra by Richard Strauss is first performed.
name: Richard Strauss

text: Vietnam War: The Pentagon tells U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson that if planned operations are to succeed, the number of American troops in Vietnam has to be increased from 120,000 to 400,000.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Pope John Paul II returns the relics of Saint John Chrysostom to the Eastern Orthodox Church.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: In Stratford-upon-Avon, William Shakespeare and Anne Hathaway pay a £40 (equivalent to £14,557 in 2023) bond in lieu of posting wedding banns, which enables them to marry immediately.
name: William Shakespeare

text: At Gresham College, twelve men, including Christopher Wren, Robert Boyle, John Wilkins, and Sir Robert Moray decide to found what is later known as the Royal Society.
name: Christopher Wren

text: World War II: Tehran Conference: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin meet in Tehran, Iran, to discuss war strategy.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Vietnam War: National Security Council members agree to recommend that U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson adopt a plan for a two-stage escalation of bombing in North Vietnam.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Vietnam War: In response to U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson's call for "more flags" in Vietnam, Philippine President-elect Ferdinand Marcos announces he will send troops to help fight in South Vietnam.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher resigns as leader of the Conservative Party and, therefore, as Prime Minister. She is succeeded in both positions by John Major.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson establishes the Warren Commission to investigate the assassination of President John F. Kennedy.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Michael Jackson releases Thriller, the best-selling music album of all time.
name: Michael Jackson

text: Henry V of England enters Paris alongside his father-in-law King Charles VI of France.
name: Charles VI of France

text: Courtiers Christopher Hatton and Thomas Heneage are knighted by Queen Elizabeth I of England.
name: Elizabeth I of England

text: American Civil War: In his second State of the Union Address, President Abraham Lincoln reaffirms the necessity of ending slavery as ordered ten weeks earlier in the Emancipation Proclamation.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Sergei Kirov is assassinated, paving way for the repressive Great Purge, and Vinnytsia massacre by General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, Joseph Stalin.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: American Civil Rights Movement: In Montgomery, Alabama, seamstress Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat to a white man and is arrested for violating the city's racial segregation laws, an incident which leads to that city's bus boycott.
name: Rosa Parks

text: Patrice Lumumba is arrested by Mobutu Sese Seko's men on the banks of the Sankuru River, for inciting the army to rebellion.
name: Mobutu Sese Seko

text: Vietnam War: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson and his top-ranking advisers meet to discuss plans to bomb North Vietnam.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 6231, another Boeing 727, crashes northwest of John F. Kennedy International Airport.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: St Paul's Cathedral, rebuilt to the design of Sir Christopher Wren following the Great Fire of London, is consecrated.
name: Christopher Wren

text: At Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris, Napoleon Bonaparte crowns himself Emperor of the French.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: At Tremont Temple in Boston, British author Charles Dickens gives his first public reading in the United States.
name: Charles Dickens

text: World War II: During the Manhattan Project, a team led by Enrico Fermi initiates the first artificial self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction.
name: Enrico Fermi

text: The Granma reaches the shores of Cuba's Oriente Province. Fidel Castro, Che Guevara and 80 other members of the 26th of July Movement disembark to initiate the Cuban Revolution.
name: Fidel Castro

text: In a nationally broadcast speech, Cuban leader Fidel Castro declares that he is a Marxist-Leninist and that Cuba will adopt Communism.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Vietnam War: After a trip to Vietnam at the request of U.S. President John F. Kennedy, U.S. Senate Majority Leader Mike Mansfield becomes the first American official to comment adversely on the war's progress.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Fidel Castro becomes President of Cuba, replacing Osvaldo Dorticós Torrado.
name: Fidel Castro

text: War of the Second Coalition: Battle of Hohenlinden: French General Jean Victor Marie Moreau decisively defeats the Archduke John of Austria near Munich. Coupled with First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte's earlier victory at Marengo, this will force the Austrians to sign an armistice and end the war.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: In a meeting off the coast of Malta, U.S. President George H. W. Bush and Soviet General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev release statements indicating that the Cold War between NATO and the Warsaw Pact may be coming to an end.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Kings Louis IX of France and Henry III of England agree to the Treaty of Paris, in which Henry renounces his claims to French-controlled territory on continental Europe (including Normandy) in exchange for Louis withdrawing his support for English rebels.
name: Henry III of England

text: At Fraunces Tavern in New York City, U.S. General George Washington bids farewell to his officers.
name: George Washington

text: World War II: In Yugoslavia, resistance leader Marshal Josip Broz Tito proclaims a provisional democratic Yugoslav government in-exile.
name: Josip Broz Tito

text: US Navy aircraft from USS John F. Kennedy and USS Independence attack Syrian missile sites in Lebanon in response to an F-14 being fired on by an SA-7. One A-6 Intruder and A-7 Corsair are shot down. One American pilot is killed, one is rescued, and one is captured.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: King Manuel I of Portugal issues a decree ordering the expulsion of Jews from the country.
name: Manuel I of Portugal

text: Thirteen-year-old Charles IX becomes king of France, with Queen Mother Catherine de' Medici as regent.
name: Catherine de' Medici

text: E. D. Nixon and Rosa Parks lead the Montgomery bus boycott.
name: Rosa Parks

text: German-born Swiss physicist Albert Einstein is granted an American visa.
name: Albert Einstein

text: Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I simultaneously revoke mutual excommunications that had been in place since 1054.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: Louis the Stammerer (son of Charles the Bald) is crowned king of the West Frankish Kingdom at Compiègne.
name: Louis the Stammerer

text: In his Apostolic constitution Ineffabilis Deus, Pope Pius IX proclaims the dogmatic definition of Immaculate Conception, which holds that the Blessed Virgin Mary was conceived free of Original Sin.
name: Pope Pius IX

text: Pope Pius IX promulgates the encyclical Quanta cura and its appendix, the Syllabus of Errors, outlining the authority of the Catholic Church and condemning various liberal ideas.
name: Pope Pius IX

text: Cold War: The Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty is signed by U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev in the White House.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: French physicist Augustin-Jean Fresnel, in a memoir read to the Academy of Sciences, coins the terms linear polarization, circular polarization, and elliptical polarization, and reports a direct refraction experiment verifying his theory that optical rotation is a form of birefringence.
name: Augustin-Jean Fresnel

text: Martin Luther burns his copy of the papal bull Exsurge Domine outside Wittenberg's Elster Gate.
name: Martin Luther

text: Isaac Newton's derivation of Kepler's laws from his theory of gravity, contained in the paper De motu corporum in gyrum, is read to the Royal Society by Edmond Halley.
name: Isaac Newton

text: The first Nobel Prize ceremony is held in Stockholm on the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.
name: Alfred Nobel

text: British Prime Minister Winston Churchill receives the Nobel Prize in Literature.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Arab-Israeli conflict: Prime Minister of Israel Menachem Begin and President of Egypt Anwar Sadat are jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
name: Menachem Begin

text: A surprise attack by forces under the command of Charles Emmanuel I, Duke of Savoy, and his brother-in-law, Philip III of Spain, is repelled by the citizens of Geneva. (Commemorated annually by the Fête de l'Escalade.)
name: Philip III of Spain

text: Glorious Revolution: James II of England, while trying to flee to France, throws the Great Seal of the Realm into the River Thames.
name: James II of England

text: French Revolution: King Louis XVI of France is put on trial for treason by the National Convention.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: Guglielmo Marconi transmits the first transatlantic radio signal from Poldhu, Cornwall, England to Saint John's, Newfoundland.
name: Guglielmo Marconi

text: Guglielmo Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal (the letter "S" [•••] in Morse Code), at Signal Hill in St John's, Newfoundland.
name: Guglielmo Marconi

text: The Lebensborn Project, a Nazi reproduction program, is founded by Heinrich Himmler.
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: The Holocaust: Adolf Hitler declares the imminent extermination of the Jews at a meeting in the Reich Chancellery.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Iraq War: Operation Red Dawn: Former Iraqi President Saddam Hussein is captured near his home town of Tikrit.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Roald Amundsen's team, comprising himself, Olav Bjaaland, Helmer Hanssen, Sverre Hassel, and Oscar Wisting, becomes the first to reach the South Pole.
name: Roald Amundsen

text: Giacomo Puccini's comic opera Gianni Schicchi premieres at the Metropolitan Opera in New York City.
name: Giacomo Puccini

text: Symphony No. 9 ("From the New World" a.k.a. the "New World Symphony") by Antonín Dvořák premieres in a public afternoon rehearsal at Carnegie Hall in New York City, followed by a concert premiere on the evening of December 16.
name: Antonín Dvořák

text: Richard Pavlick is arrested for plotting to assassinate U.S. President-Elect John F. Kennedy.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Eichmann trial: Adolf Eichmann is sentenced to death after being found guilty by an Israeli court of 15 criminal charges, including charges of crimes against humanity, crimes against the Jewish people, and membership of an outlawed organization.
name: Adolf Eichmann

text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter announces that the United States will recognize the People's Republic of China and sever diplomatic relations with the Republic of China (Taiwan).
name: Jimmy Carter

text: English Interregnum: The Protectorate: Oliver Cromwell becomes Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland.
name: Oliver Cromwell

text: The Holocaust: Schutzstaffel chief Heinrich Himmler orders that Roma candidates for extermination be deported to Auschwitz.
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: Jeltoqsan: Riots erupt in Alma-Ata, Kazakh SSR, in response to Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev's dismissal of ethnic Kazakh Dinmukhamed Kunaev, the First Secretary of the Communist Party of Kazakhstan, and his replacement with Gennady Kolbin, an ethnic Russian from the Russian SFSR.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Pope Paul III excommunicates Henry VIII of England.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: The first account of a blood transfusion is published, in the form of a letter from physician Richard Lower to chemist Robert Boyle, in Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society
name: Robert Boyle

text: Simón Bolívar declares the independence of Gran Colombia in Angostura (now Ciudad Bolívar in Venezuela).
name: Simón Bolívar

text: First performance of the Unfinished Symphony by Franz Schubert.
name: Franz Schubert

text: Fernando Collor de Mello defeats Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the second round of the Brazilian presidential election, becoming the first democratically elected President in almost 30 years.
name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva

text: Kublai Khan renames his empire "Yuan" (元 yuán), officially marking the start of the Yuan dynasty of Mongolia and China.
name: Kublai Khan

text: Premiere performance of The Nutcracker by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
name: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky

text: Henry II of England is crowned at Westminster Abbey.
name: Henry II of England

text: American Revolutionary War: George Washington's Continental Army goes into winter quarters at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania.
name: George Washington

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler appoints himself as head of the Oberkommando des Heeres.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: The Sino-British Joint Declaration, stating that China would resume the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong and the United Kingdom would restore Hong Kong to China with effect from July 1, 1997, is signed in Beijing by Deng Xiaoping and Margaret Thatcher.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: Mikhail Gorbachev, leader of the Soviet Union, releases Andrei Sakharov and his wife from exile in Gorky.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Richard I of England is captured and imprisoned by Leopold V of Austria on his way home to England after the Third Crusade.
name: Richard I of England

text: French presidential election: Having won the popular vote in a landslide, Louis Napoleon Bonaparte is inaugurated in the chamber of the National Assembly as the first (and only) president of the French Second Republic.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Adolf Hitler is released from Landsberg Prison.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Pope John Paul II announces the institution of World Youth Day.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Medal of Honor: Public Resolution 82, containing a provision for a Navy Medal of Valor, is signed into law by President Abraham Lincoln.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: The Turkish fortress of Izmail is stormed and captured by Alexander Suvorov and his Russian armies.
name: Alexander Suvorov

text: Ludwig van Beethoven conducts and performs in concert at the Theater an der Wien, Vienna, with the premiere of his Fifth Symphony, Sixth Symphony, Fourth Piano Concerto and Choral Fantasy.
name: Ludwig van Beethoven

text: American Civil War: Savannah, Georgia, falls to the Union's Army of the Tennessee, and General Sherman tells President Abraham Lincoln: "I beg to present you as a Christmas gift the city of Savannah".
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Itō Hirobumi, a samurai, becomes the first Prime Minister of Japan.
name: Itō Hirobumi

text: The Dreyfus affair begins in France, when Alfred Dreyfus is wrongly convicted of treason.
name: Alfred Dreyfus

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler signs the order to develop the V-2 rocket as a weapon.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: The pivotal Third Plenum of the 11th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party is held in Beijing, with Deng Xiaoping reversing Mao-era policies to pursue a program for Chinese economic reform.
name: Deng Xiaoping

text: Lech Wałęsa is elected President of Poland.
name: Lech Wałęsa

text: As part of the Glorious Revolution, King James II of England flees from England to Paris after being deposed in favor of his son-in-law and nephew, William of Orange and his daughter Mary.
name: James II of England

text: George Washington resigns as commander-in-chief of the Continental Army at the Maryland State House in Annapolis, Maryland.
name: George Washington

text: The novel Emma by Jane Austen is first published.
name: Jane Austen

text: The Tampere conference, where Vladimir Lenin and Joseph Stalin meet for the first time, is held in Tampere, Finland.
name: Vladimir Lenin

text: Kiritimati, also called Christmas Island, is discovered by James Cook.
name: James Cook

text: The Plot of the rue Saint-Nicaise fails to kill Napoleon Bonaparte.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: World War II: Pope Pius XII makes a Christmas Eve appeal for peace.
name: Pope Pius XII

text: Count Roger II of Sicily is crowned the first king of Sicily.
name: Roger II of Sicily

text: Pope Pius IV is elected, four months after his predecessor's death.
name: Pope Pius IV

text: American Revolutionary War: General George Washington and the Continental Army cross the Delaware River at night to attack Hessian forces serving Great Britain at Trenton, New Jersey, the next day.
name: George Washington

text: Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin meets in Egypt with its president Anwar Sadat.
name: Menachem Begin

text: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as President of the Soviet Union (the union itself is dissolved the next day). Ukraine's referendum is finalized and Ukraine officially leaves the Soviet Union.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: The opera Agrippina by George Frideric Handel premiered in Venice.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: American Revolutionary War: In the Battle of Trenton, the Continental Army under General George Washington executes a successful surprise attack and defeats a garrison of Hessian forces serving Great Britain.
name: George Washington

text: Louis XVI of France gives his public assent to Civil Constitution of the Clergy during the French Revolution.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: Henry Lee III's eulogy to George Washington in congress declares him as "first in war, first in peace and first in the hearts of his countrymen".
name: George Washington

text: Marie and Pierre Curie announce the isolation of radium.
name: Pierre Curie

text: British Prime Minister Winston Churchill addresses a joint meeting of the U.S. Congress.
name: Winston Churchill

text: World War II: George S. Patton's Third Army breaks the encirclement of surrounded U.S. forces at Bastogne, Belgium.
name: George S. Patton

text: Charles Darwin embarks on his journey aboard HMS Beagle, during which he will begin to formulate his theory of evolution.
name: Charles Darwin

text: Soviet General Secretary Joseph Stalin orders the "liquidation of the kulaks as a class".
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Pope John Paul II visits Mehmet Ali Ağca in Rebibbia's prison and personally forgives him for the 1981 attack on him in St. Peter's Square.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: World War II: Operation Anthropoid, the plot to assassinate high-ranking Nazi officer Reinhard Heydrich, commences.
name: Reinhard Heydrich

text: Reapers' War: Louis XIII of France swears the Catalan constitutions, being appointed Count of Barcelona and thus establishing the personal union of the Principality of Catalonia with the Kingdom of France.
name: Louis XIII of France

text: Former President of Iraq Saddam Hussein is executed.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: American Civil War: Abraham Lincoln signs an enabling act that would admit West Virginia to the Union, thus dividing Virginia in two.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: World War II: The Royal Navy defeats the Kriegsmarine at the Battle of the Barents Sea. This leads to the resignation of Grand Admiral Erich Raeder a month later.
name: Erich Raeder

text: The first President of Russia, Boris Yeltsin, resigns from office, leaving Prime Minister Vladimir Putin as the acting President and successor.
name: Vladimir Putin
